celaleyn:118-118.t: ﴿لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ﴾ removed him far from His mercy ﴿وَقَالَ﴾ i.e. Satan ﴿لَأَتَّخِذَنَّ﴾ I shall surely make for myself ﴿مِنْ عِبَادِكَ نَصِيبًا﴾ a share ﴿مَفْرُوضًا﴾ allotted, whom I call to obey me

celaleyn:119-119.t: ﴿وَلَأُضِلَّنَّهُمْ﴾ from the truth by whispering ﴿وَلَأُمَنِّيَنَّهُمْ﴾ I will cast into their hearts [hope of] long life, and that there is no resurrection and no reckoning ﴿وَلَآمُرَنَّهُمْ فَلَيُبَتِّكُنَّ﴾ cut off ﴿آذَانَ الْأَنْعَامِ﴾ and that was done to the baḥīras ﴿وَلَآمُرَنَّهُمْ فَلَيُغَيِّرُنَّ خَلْقَ اللَّهِ﴾ His religion, by disbelief, making lawful what Allah has forbidden and forbidding what He has made lawful ﴿وَمَنْ يَتَّخِذِ الشَّيْطَانَ وَلِيًّا﴾ taking him as patron and obeying him ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿فَقَدْ خَسِرَ خُسْرَانًا مُبِينًا﴾ clear, because of his destination to the Fire, made everlasting upon him

celaleyn:120-120.t: ﴿يَعِدُهُمْ﴾ long life ﴿وَيُمَنِّيهِمْ﴾ the attaining of hopes in this world, and that there is no resurrection and no recompense ﴿وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ﴾ with that ﴿إِلَّا غُرُورًا﴾ falsehood

celaleyn:121-121.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَلَا يَجِدُونَ عَنْهَا مَحِيصًا﴾ a way of escape.

celaleyn:122-122.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ سَنُدْخِلُهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقًّا﴾ i.e. Allah promised them that, and made it true truly ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ i.e. no one ﴿أَصْدَقُ مِنَ اللَّهِ قِيلًا﴾ i.e. in speech. And [the following] was revealed when the Muslims and the People of the Book boasted [to each other]

celaleyn:123-123.t: ﴿لَيْسَ﴾ the matter dependent ﴿بِأَمَانِيِّكُمْ وَلَا أَمَانِيِّ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ﴾ but rather on righteous action ﴿مَنْ يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا يُجْزَ بِهِ﴾ either in the Hereafter, or in this world by affliction and trials, as has come in the hadith ﴿وَلَا يَجِدْ لَهُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿وَلِيًّا﴾ who protects him ﴿وَلَا نَصِيرًا﴾ who defends him from it

celaleyn:124-124.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ﴾ anything ﴿مِنَ الصَّالِحَاتِ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَى وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَأُولَئِكَ يَدْخَلُونَ﴾ in the passive and the active [يَدْخُلُونَ] ﴿الْجَنَّةَ وَلَا يُظْلَمُونَ نَقِيرًا﴾ the measure of the speck on a date-stone

celaleyn:125-125.t: ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ i.e. no one ﴿أَحْسَنُ دِينًا مِمَّنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ﴾ i.e. submitted and made his deeds sincere ﴿لِلَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ﴾ affirming [Allah's] oneness ﴿وَاتَّبَعَ مِلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ which accords with the creed of Islam ﴿حَنِيفًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. inclining away from all religions to the upright religion ﴿وَاتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ خَلِيلًا﴾ a chosen one, pure in love for Him

celaleyn:126-126.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ as dominion, creation and servants ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُحِيطًا﴾ in knowledge and power, i.e. He has never ceased to be characterised by that

celaleyn:127-127.t: ﴿وَيَسْتَفْتُونَكَ﴾ they seek a ruling from you ﴿فِي﴾ the matter of ﴿النِّسَاءِ﴾ and their inheritance ﴿قُلِ﴾ to them ﴿اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ وَمَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Quran, of the ayah of inheritance, also gives you a ruling ﴿فِي يَتَامَى النِّسَاءِ الَّتِي لَا تُؤْتُونَهُنَّ مَا كُتِبَ﴾ was made obligatory ﴿لَهُنَّ﴾ of inheritance ﴿وَتَرْغَبُونَ﴾ O guardians, [averse] to [عَنْ] ﴿أَنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ﴾ because of their unattractiveness, and you prevent them from marrying out of greed for their inheritance; i.e. He gives you a ruling that you are not to do that ﴿وَ﴾ concerning [فِي] ﴿الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ﴾ the young ﴿مِنَ الْوِلْدَانِ﴾ that you give them their rights ﴿وَ﴾ He commands you ﴿أَنْ تَقُومُوا لِلْيَتَامَى بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ with justice in inheritance and dower ﴿وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِهِ عَلِيمًا﴾ so He will requite you for it.

celaleyn:128-128.t: ﴿وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ﴾ nominative by a verb which is explained by ﴿خَافَتْ﴾ anticipated ﴿مِنْ بَعْلِهَا﴾ her husband ﴿نُشُوزًا﴾ his haughtiness toward her, by ceasing to share her bed and falling short in her maintenance, out of dislike for her and his eye straying to one more beautiful than her ﴿أَوْ إِعْرَاضًا﴾ turning his face away from her ﴿فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا أَنْ يَصَّالَحَا﴾ in it there is assimilation (idghām) of the original tāʾ into the ṣād; and in one reading [يُصْلِحَا], from أَصْلَحَ ﴿بَيْنَهُمَا صُلْحًا﴾ in the division [of nights] and maintenance, by her giving up something to him, seeking that the companionship continue; if she is content with that [so be it]; otherwise the husband must give her her full right or separate from her ﴿وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾ than separation, haughtiness and turning away. Allah the Exalted said, explaining what the human being is innately disposed to: ﴿وَأُحْضِرَتِ الْأَنْفُسُ الشُّحَّ﴾ intense avarice, i.e. they are innately disposed to it, as if it were present with them and never absent from them. The meaning is that the woman hardly ever gives up her share of her husband, and the man hardly ever gives himself generously to her when he loves another ﴿وَإِنْ تُحْسِنُوا﴾ in living with women ﴿وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ injustice toward them ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ so He will requite you for it

celaleyn:129-129.t: ﴿وَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعُوا أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا﴾ make equal ﴿بَيْنَ النِّسَاءِ﴾ in love ﴿وَلَوْ حَرَصْتُمْ﴾ on that ﴿فَلَا تَمِيلُوا كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ﴾ to the one you love in the division [of nights] and maintenance ﴿فَتَذَرُوهَا﴾ i.e. leave the one turned away from ﴿كَالْمُعَلَّقَةِ﴾ who is neither unmarried nor has a husband ﴿وَإِنْ تُصْلِحُوا﴾ by justice in the division ﴿وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ injustice ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورًا﴾ of the inclination in your hearts ﴿رَحِيمًا﴾ to you in that

celaleyn:130-130.t: ﴿وَإِنْ يَتَفَرَّقَا﴾ i.e. the spouses, by divorce ﴿يُغْنِ اللَّهُ كُلًّا﴾ [making each] independent of the other ﴿مِنْ سَعَتِهِ﴾ i.e. His bounty, by providing her with another husband and him with another [wife] ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ وَاسِعًا﴾ in bounty to His creation ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in what He has arranged for them

celaleyn:131-131.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَقَدْ وَصَّيْنَا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ﴾ in the sense of the Books ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ i.e. the Jews and the Christians ﴿وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾ O people of the Quran ﴿أَنِ﴾ i.e. بِأَنِ ﴿اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ fear His punishment by obeying Him ﴿وَ﴾ We said to them and to you ﴿إِنْ تَكْفُرُوا﴾ in what you were enjoined with ﴿فَإِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ as creation, dominion and servants, so your disbelief does not harm Him ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَنِيًّا﴾ independent of His creation and their worship ﴿حَمِيدًا﴾ praised in what He does with them

celaleyn:132-132.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ He repeated it for emphasis, to establish what necessitates godfearingness ﴿وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا﴾ a witness that what is in them belongs to Him

celaleyn:133-133.t: ﴿إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ﴾ O [يَا] ﴿أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ وَيَأْتِ بِآخَرِينَ﴾ in your place ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ قَدِيرًا﴾

celaleyn:134-134.t: ﴿وَمَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ﴾ by his deeds ﴿ثَوَابَ الدُّنْيَا فَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ ثَوَابُ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ for whoever wants it, not with anyone else; so why does one of them seek the baser, and why does he not seek the higher with sincerity toward Him, since what he seeks is found only with Him? ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا﴾.

celaleyn:135-135.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ﴾ standing firm ﴿بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ with justice ﴿شُهَدَاءَ﴾ to the truth ﴿لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ﴾ the testimony be ﴿عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ then testify against them, by acknowledging the truth and not concealing it ﴿أَوْ﴾ against [عَلَى] ﴿الْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ إِنْ يَكُنْ﴾ the one testified against ﴿غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًا فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِهِمَا﴾ than you, and knows better their interests ﴿فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا الْهَوَى﴾ in your testimony, by favouring the rich to please him, or the poor out of pity for him, so [لِ] ﴿أَنْ﴾ not [لَا] ﴿تَعْدِلُوا﴾ swerve from the truth ﴿وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا﴾ distort the testimony — and in one reading with omission of the first wāw for lightening ﴿أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا﴾ from giving it ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ so He will requite you for it

celaleyn:136-136.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا﴾ persevere in faith ﴿بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي نُزِّلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ﴾ Muhammad ﷺ, and it is the Quran ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ upon the messengers, in the sense of the Books; and in one reading with the active form in both verbs [نَزَّلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ...أَنْزَلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ] ﴿وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ from the truth

celaleyn:137-137.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ in Moses — and they are the Jews ﴿ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا﴾ by worshipping the calf ﴿ثُمَّ آمَنُوا﴾ after it ﴿ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا﴾ in Jesus ﴿ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا﴾ in Muhammad ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ as long as they persist in it ﴿وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ a path to the truth

celaleyn:138-138.t: ﴿بَشِّرْ﴾ inform, O Muhammad ﴿الْمُنَافِقِينَ بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ painful; it is the punishment of the Fire

celaleyn:139-139.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a badal (substitute) or naʿt (adjective) of الْمُنَافِقِينَ ﴿يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ because of the strength they imagine in them ﴿أَيَبْتَغُونَ﴾ seek ﴿عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ﴾ a question of denial (inkār), i.e. they will not find it with them ﴿فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ in this world and the Hereafter, and none attains it but His friends

celaleyn:140-140.t: ﴿وَقَدْ نَزَّلَ﴾ with the active and the passive form ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Quran, in Sūrat al-Anʿām ﴿أَنْ﴾ lightened (mukhaffafa), and its noun is omitted, i.e. أَنَّهُ ﴿إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ the Quran ﴿يُكْفَرُ بِهَا وَيُسْتَهْزَأُ بِهَا فَلَا تَقْعُدُوا مَعَهُمْ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers and the mockers ﴿حَتَّى يَخُوضُوا فِي حَدِيثٍ غَيْرِهِ إِنَّكُمْ إِذًا﴾ if you sit with them ﴿مِثْلُهُمْ﴾ in sin ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ جَامِعُ الْمُنَافِقِينَ وَالْكَافِرِينَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ جَمِيعًا﴾ just as they gathered in this world upon disbelief and mockery.

celaleyn:141-141.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a badal (substitute) of the الَّذِينَ before it ﴿يَتَرَبَّصُونَ﴾ wait ﴿بِكُمْ﴾ for misfortunes ﴿فَإِنْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فَتْحٌ﴾ victory and spoils ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ قَالُوا﴾ to you ﴿أَلَمْ نَكُنْ مَعَكُمْ﴾ in religion and jihad? So give us of the spoils ﴿وَإِنْ كَانَ لِلْكَافِرِينَ نَصِيبٌ﴾ of victory over you ﴿قَالُوا﴾ to them ﴿أَلَمْ نَسْتَحْوِذْ﴾ gain mastery ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ and were able to capture and kill you, yet we spared you ﴿وَ﴾ did we not [أَلَمْ] ﴿نَمْنَعْكُمْ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ from their prevailing over you, by discouraging them and sending you their news? So we have done you a favour. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿فَاللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ and them ﴿يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾ by admitting you into Paradise and them into the Fire ﴿وَلَنْ يَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ سَبِيلًا﴾ a way to extermination

celaleyn:142-142.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُنَافِقِينَ يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ﴾ by displaying the opposite of the disbelief they conceal, so as to ward off its worldly rulings from themselves ﴿وَهُوَ خَادِعُهُمْ﴾ requites them for their deception: they are exposed in this world by Allah's informing His Prophet of what they concealed, and they are punished in the Hereafter ﴿وَإِذَا قَامُوا إِلَى الصَّلَوةِ﴾ with the believers ﴿قَامُوا كُسَالَى﴾ sluggish ﴿يُرَاءُونَ النَّاسَ﴾ with their prayer ﴿وَلَا يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ﴾ they do not pray ﴿إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾ for show

celaleyn:143-143.t: ﴿مُذَبْذَبِينَ﴾ wavering ﴿بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ﴾ disbelief and faith ﴿لَا﴾ affiliated ﴿إِلَى هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers ﴿وَلَا إِلَى هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ i.e. the believers ﴿وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ﴾ him [هُ] ﴿اللَّهُ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُ سَبِيلًا﴾ a path to guidance

celaleyn:144-144.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَّخِذُوا الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَتُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَجْعَلُوا لِلَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ by befriending them ﴿سُلْطَانًا مُبِينًا﴾ a clear proof of your hypocrisy

celaleyn:145-145.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُنَافِقِينَ فِي الدَّرْكِ﴾ the place ﴿الْأَسْفَلِ مِنَ النَّارِ﴾ and it is its bottom ﴿وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُمْ نَصِيرًا﴾ a defender from the punishment

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ﴾ i.e. the people of Mecca ﴿اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ﴾ i.e. His punishment, by obeying Him ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ﴾ Ādam ﴿وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا﴾ Ḥawwāʾ (with the long vowel), from one of his left ribs ﴿وَبَثَّ﴾ dispersed and spread ﴿مِنْهُمَا﴾ from Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ ﴿رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا وَنِسَاءً﴾ many ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسَاءَلُونَ﴾ in it the tāʾ of the original form is assimilated (idghām) into the sīn; and in one reading [تَسَاءَلُونَ] it is with the light form, by omitting it, i.e. تَتَسَاءَلُونَ ﴿بِهِ﴾ among yourselves, when one of you says to another: "I ask you by Allah" and "I adjure you by Allah" ﴿وَ﴾ fear ﴿الْأَرْحَامَ﴾ lest you sever them; and in one reading it is in the genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the pronoun in بِهِ, for they used to adjure one another by kinship ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا﴾ guarding your deeds, so He will recompense you for them, i.e. He has always been characterised by that. And the following was revealed concerning an orphan who asked his guardian for his property and he refused him:

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَآتُوا الْيَتَامَى﴾ the young who have no father ﴿أَمْوَالَهُمْ﴾ when they come of age ﴿وَلَا تَتَبَدَّلُوا الْخَبِيثَ﴾ the unlawful ﴿بِالطَّيِّبِ﴾ the lawful, i.e. take it in its place, as you do in taking the good from the orphan's property and putting the bad from your own property in its place ﴿وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَهُمْ﴾ joined ﴿إِلَى أَمْوَالِكُمْ إِنَّهُ﴾ i.e. consuming it ﴿كَانَ حُوبًا﴾ a sin ﴿كَبِيرًا﴾ great. When it was revealed they felt constrained about guardianship of orphans, and among them were those who had ten or eight wives and did not deal justly between them, so the following was revealed:

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا تُقْسِطُوا﴾ deal justly ﴿فِي الْيَتَامَى﴾ and so felt constrained in their matter, then fear also that you will not deal justly between women when you marry them ﴿فَانْكِحُوا﴾ marry ﴿مَا﴾ in the sense of مَنْ ("whoever") ﴿طَابَ لَكُمْ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ مَثْنَى وَثُلَاثَ وَرُبَاعَ﴾ i.e. two at a time, three at a time and four at a time, and do not exceed that ﴿فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا﴾ among them in maintenance and division [Translator's note: of nights] ﴿فَوَاحِدَةً﴾ marry her ﴿أَوْ﴾ restrict yourselves to ﴿مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ﴾ of slave-women, since they do not have the rights that wives have ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. marrying four only, or one, or taking concubines ﴿أَدْنَى﴾ nearer to ﴿أَلَّا تَعُولُوا﴾ act unjustly

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَآتُوا﴾ give ﴿النِّسَاءَ صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ﴾ plural of صَدُقَة: their bridal dowries ﴿نِحْلَةً﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun): a gift given willingly ﴿فَإِنْ طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ نَفْسًا﴾ a tamyīz (specification) transposed from the fāʿil (agent), i.e. their souls are pleased to give you something of the dowry and so they gift it to you ﴿فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيئًا﴾ wholesome ﴿مَرِيئًا﴾ of praiseworthy outcome, with no harm in it for you in the Hereafter. It was revealed in refutation of those who disliked that

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَلَا تُؤْتُوا﴾ O guardians ﴿السُّفَهَاءَ﴾ the squanderers among men, women and children ﴿أَمْوَالَكُمْ﴾ i.e. their property which is in your hands ﴿الَّتِي جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ قِيَامًا﴾ a maṣdar of قَامَ, i.e. it sustains your livelihood and sets right your crookedness, for they would put it in the wrong place; and in one reading [قِيَمًا], plural of قِيمَة: that by which goods are valued ﴿وَارْزُقُوهُمْ فِيهَا﴾ feed them from it ﴿وَاكْسُوهُمْ وَقُولُوا لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفًا﴾ give them a fair promise that you will give them their property when they become mature

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَابْتَلُوا﴾ test ﴿الْيَتَامَى﴾ before puberty, in their religion and in their handling of their affairs ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا بَلَغُوا النِّكَاحَ﴾ i.e. become fit for it, through wet dreams or age, which is the completion of fifteen years according to al-Shāfiʿī ﴿فَإِنْ آنَسْتُمْ﴾ you perceive ﴿مِنْهُمْ رُشْدًا﴾ soundness in their religion and their property ﴿فَادْفَعُوا إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوَالَهُمْ وَلَا تَأْكُلُوهَا﴾ O guardians ﴿إِسْرَافًا﴾ without right; a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿وَبِدَارًا﴾ i.e. hastening to spend it, for fear ﴿أَنْ يَكْبَرُوا﴾ mature, and you would then be obliged to hand it over to them ﴿وَمَنْ كَانَ﴾ of the guardians ﴿غَنِيًّا فَلْيَسْتَعْفِفْ﴾ i.e. abstain from the orphan's property and refrain from consuming it ﴿وَمَنْ كَانَ فَقِيرًا فَلْيَأْكُلْ﴾ of it ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ to the extent of the wage for his work ﴿فَإِذَا دَفَعْتُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ i.e. to the orphans ﴿أَمْوَالَهُمْ فَأَشْهِدُوا عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ that they have received it and you are cleared, lest a dispute arise and you have recourse to evidence; and this command is guidance (irshād) ﴿وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ﴾ the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) ﴿حَسِيبًا﴾ guarding the deeds of His creation and taking them to account

celaleyn:7-7.t: And the following was revealed in refutation of the practice of the Jāhiliyya of not giving women and young children inheritance: ﴿لِلرِّجَالِ﴾ the children and relatives ﴿نَصِيبٌ﴾ a share ﴿مِمَّا تَرَكَ الْوَالِدَانِ وَالْأَقْرَبُونَ﴾ who have died ﴿وَلِلنِّسَاءِ نَصِيبٌ مِمَّا تَرَكَ الْوَالِدَانِ وَالْأَقْرَبُونَ مِمَّا قَلَّ مِنْهُ﴾ i.e. of the wealth ﴿أَوْ كَثُرَ﴾ Allah has made it ﴿نَصِيبًا مَفْرُوضًا﴾ definitively due to be handed over to them

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَإِذَا حَضَرَ الْقِسْمَةَ﴾ of the inheritance ﴿أُولُوا الْقُرْبَى﴾ relatives who do not inherit ﴿وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينُ فَارْزُقُوهُمْ مِنْهُ﴾ something, before the division ﴿وَقُولُوا﴾ O guardians ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ if the heirs are minors ﴿قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفًا﴾ kind, by apologising to them that you do not own it and that it belongs to the minors. Of this it has been said that it is abrogated, and it has been said: no, but people have been lax in neglecting it; on this view it is recommended (nadb). And from Ibn ʿAbbās: it is obligatory

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَلْيَخْشَ﴾ i.e. let them fear for the orphans ﴿الَّذِينَ لَوْ تَرَكُوا﴾ i.e. were near to leaving ﴿مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ﴾ i.e. after their death ﴿ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعَافًا﴾ young children ﴿خَافُوا عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ loss ﴿فَلْيَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ in the matter of the orphans, and let them do to them what they would like to be done to their own offspring after them ﴿وَلْيَقُولُوا﴾ to the dying person ﴿قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا﴾ right, by telling him to give in charity less than his third and leave the rest to his heirs, and not leave them dependent on others

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوَالَ الْيَتَامَى ظُلْمًا﴾ without right ﴿إِنَّمَا يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ﴾ i.e. their fill ﴿نَارًا﴾ because it leads to it ﴿وَسَيَصْلَوْنَ﴾ in the active and the passive: they will enter ﴿سَعِيرًا﴾ an intense fire in which they burn

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿يُوصِيكُمُ﴾ commands you ﴿اللَّهُ فِي﴾ the matter of ﴿أَوْلَادِكُمْ﴾ with what is mentioned: ﴿لِلذَّكَرِ﴾ among them ﴿مِثْلُ حَظِّ﴾ the share of ﴿الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ﴾ when two are together with him, so he has half the wealth and they have half; if there is one with him, she has a third and he has two thirds; and if he is alone, he takes all the wealth ﴿فَإِنْ كُنَّ﴾ i.e. the children ﴿نِسَاءً﴾ only ﴿فَوْقَ اثْنَتَيْنِ فَلَهُنَّ ثُلُثَا مَا تَرَكَ﴾ the deceased; and likewise two, because it belongs to two sisters by His saying {فَلَهُمَا الثُّلُثَانِ مِمَّا تَرَكَ} ("then they have two thirds of what he left"), so they [Translator's note: the two daughters] have more right; and because a daughter is entitled to a third along with a male, so with a female she is even more entitled. As for {وَفَوْقَ}, it has been said that it is a connective (ṣila) [Translator's note: i.e. redundant], and it has been said that it is to prevent the supposition that the share increases with the increase in number, since the entitlement of two daughters to two thirds is understood from assigning a third to the one with a male ﴿وَإِنْ كَانَتْ﴾ the daughter ﴿وَاحِدَةً﴾ and in one reading in the nominative, so كَانَ is complete (tāmma) ﴿فَلَهَا النِّصْفُ وَلِأَبَوَيْهِ﴾ i.e. of the deceased; and substituted (badal) from them is ﴿لِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا السُّدُسُ مِمَّا تَرَكَ إِنْ كَانَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ﴾ male or female. The subtle point of the badal is to convey that they do not share in it [Translator's note: i.e. each has a full sixth]. The son's child is assimilated to the child, and the grandfather to the father ﴿فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ وَلَدٌ وَوَرِثَهُ أَبَوَاهُ﴾ alone or with a spouse ﴿فَلِأُمِّهِ﴾ with ḍamma and kasra on the hamza, [Translator's note: the latter] to avoid passing from a ḍamma to a kasra because of its heaviness, in both places ﴿الثُّلُثُ﴾ i.e. a third of the wealth, or of what remains after the spouse, and the rest is for the father ﴿فَإِنْ كَانَ لَهُ إِخْوَةٌ﴾ i.e. two or more, male or female ﴿فَلِأُمِّهِ السُّدُسُ﴾ and the rest is for the father, and nothing for the siblings. And the inheritance of those mentioned, of what is mentioned, is ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ executing ﴿وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصِي﴾ in the active and the passive ﴿بِهَا أَوْ﴾ paying ﴿دَيْنٍ﴾ owed by him. The bequest is placed before the debt, though it comes after it in settlement, to give it importance ﴿آبَاؤُكُمْ وَأَبْنَاؤُكُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿لَا تَدْرُونَ أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ لَكُمْ نَفْعًا﴾ in this world and the Hereafter: one thinks his son is more beneficial to him and gives him the inheritance, and the father turns out more beneficial, and vice versa. Only Allah knows that, so He has prescribed the inheritance for you ﴿فَرِيضَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا﴾ of His creation ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in what He has arranged for them, i.e. He has always been characterised by that

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَلَكُمْ نِصْفُ مَا تَرَكَ أَزْوَاجُكُمْ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُنَّ وَلَدٌ﴾ by you or by others ﴿فَإِنْ كَانَ لَهُنَّ وَلَدٌ فَلَكُمُ الرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكْنَ مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصِينَ بِهَا أَوْ دَيْنٍ﴾ and the son's child is assimilated to the child in this by consensus (ijmāʿ) ﴿وَلَهُنَّ﴾ i.e. the wives, whether several or not ﴿الرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكْتُمْ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَكُمْ وَلَدٌ فَإِنْ كَانَ لَكُمْ وَلَدٌ﴾ by them or by others ﴿فَلَهُنَّ الثُّمُنُ مِمَّا تَرَكْتُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ تُوصُونَ بِهَا أَوْ دَيْنٍ﴾ and the son's child in this is like the child, by consensus ﴿وَإِنْ كَانَ رَجُلٌ يُورَثُ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa), and the khabar (predicate) is ﴿كَلَالَةً﴾ i.e. he has neither parent nor child ﴿أَوِ امْرَأَةٌ﴾ inherited from as kalāla ﴿وَلَهُ﴾ i.e. the one inherited from as kalāla ﴿أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌ﴾ i.e. from the mother, and Ibn Masʿūd and others read it so ﴿فَلِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا السُّدُسُ﴾ of what he left ﴿فَإِنْ كَانُوا﴾ i.e. the brothers and sisters from the mother ﴿أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. than one ﴿فَهُمْ شُرَكَاءُ فِي الثُّلُثِ﴾ their males and females being equal in it ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصَى بِهَا أَوْ دَيْنٍ غَيْرَ مُضَارٍّ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of يُوصَى, i.e. not bringing harm upon the heirs by bequeathing more than a third ﴿وَصِيَّةً﴾ an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun) for يُوصِيكُمْ ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ﴾ of the shares He has arranged for His creation ﴿حَلِيمٌ﴾ in deferring punishment from those who oppose Him. The Sunna has restricted the inheritance of those mentioned to those in whom there is no impediment such as killing, difference of religion or slavery

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ rulings mentioned, concerning the orphans and what follows ﴿حُدُودُ اللَّهِ﴾ His laws which He has set for His servants to act upon and not transgress ﴿وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ in what He has ruled ﴿يُدْخِلْهُ﴾ with yāʾ and with nūn, as a shift (iltifāt) ﴿جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَذَلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ﴾

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَيَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَهُ يُدْخِلْهُ﴾ in both ways ﴿نَارًا خَالِدًا فِيهَا وَلَهُ﴾ in it ﴿عَذَابٌ مُهِينٌ﴾ involving humiliation. In the pronouns in the two ayahs the wording of مَنْ is taken into account, and in خَالِدِينَ its meaning.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَالَّتِي يَأْتِينَ الْفَاحِشَةَ﴾ fornication ﴿مِنْ نِسَائِكُمْ فَاسْتَشْهِدُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ أَرْبَعَةً مِنْكُمْ﴾ i.e. from among your Muslim men ﴿فَإِنْ شَهِدُوا﴾ against them of it ﴿فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ﴾ confine them ﴿فِي الْبُيُوتِ﴾ and prevent them from mixing with people ﴿حَتَّى يَتَوَفَّاهُنَّ الْمَوْتُ﴾ i.e. its angels ﴿أَوْ﴾ until ﴿أَنْ يَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ لَهُنَّ سَبِيلًا﴾ a way out of it. They were commanded this at the beginning of Islam; then a way was made for them: flogging the unmarried woman a hundred [Translator's note: lashes] and exiling her for a year, and stoning the muḥṣana (married woman). And in the hadith, when he explained the ḥadd punishment, he said: "Take from me, take from me: Allah has made a way for them." Narrated by Muslim. [Translator's note: the source text writes the Quranic word as وَالَّتِي; the muṣḥaf reads وَاللَّاتِي.]

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَالَّذَانِ﴾ with the nūn light and doubled ﴿يَأْتِيَانِهَا﴾ i.e. the lewdness, fornication or sodomy ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ i.e. of the men ﴿فَآذُوهُمَا﴾ by insult and beating with sandals ﴿فَإِنْ تَابَا﴾ from it ﴿وَأَصْلَحَا﴾ their conduct ﴿فَأَعْرِضُوا عَنْهُمَا﴾ and do not harm them ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ تَوَّابًا﴾ towards whoever repents ﴿رَحِيمًا﴾ to him. This is abrogated by the ḥadd if fornication is meant by it, and likewise if sodomy is meant by it according to al-Shāfiʿī; but according to him the passive partner is not stoned even if muḥṣan, rather he is flogged and exiled. That sodomy is meant is more apparent, as evidenced by the dual pronoun; and the one who held the first view said that the fornicator and the fornicatress are meant, but this is refuted by their being specified by مِنْ attached to the pronoun of the men, and by their sharing in the harm, the repentance and the turning away, which is specific to men, given the confinement mentioned before for women

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا التَّوْبَةُ عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. that which He has by His bounty written upon Himself to accept ﴿لِلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السُّوءَ﴾ disobedience ﴿بِجَهَالَةٍ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. being ignorant when they disobeyed their Lord ﴿ثُمَّ يَتُوبُونَ مِنْ﴾ a time ﴿قَرِيبٍ﴾ before the death-rattle ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ يَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ accepts their repentance ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا﴾ of His creation ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in His dealing with them

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿وَلَيْسَتِ التَّوْبَةُ لِلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السَّيِّئَاتِ﴾ sins ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَهُمُ الْمَوْتُ﴾ and he begins the throes of death ﴿قَالَ﴾ upon seeing what he is in ﴿إِنِّي تُبْتُ الْآنَ﴾ so that does not benefit him and is not accepted from him ﴿وَلَا الَّذِينَ يَمُوتُونَ وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ﴾ if they repent in the Hereafter upon seeing the punishment, it is not accepted from them ﴿أُولَئِكَ أَعْتَدْنَا﴾ We have prepared ﴿لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ painful

celaleyn:146-146.t: ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا﴾ from hypocrisy ﴿وَأَصْلَحُوا﴾ their deeds ﴿وَاعْتَصَمُوا﴾ trusted ﴿بِاللَّهِ وَأَخْلَصُوا دِينَهُمْ لِلَّهِ﴾ from showing off ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ مَعَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ in what they are given ﴿وَسَوْفَ يُؤْتِ اللَّهُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾ in the Hereafter; it is Paradise

celaleyn:147-147.t: ﴿مَا يَفْعَلُ اللَّهُ بِعَذَابِكُمْ إِنْ شَكَرْتُمْ﴾ His blessings ﴿وَآمَنْتُمْ﴾ in Him; the question has the sense of negation, i.e. He will not punish you ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ شَاكِرًا﴾ of the deeds of the believers, by rewarding [them] ﴿عَلِيمًا﴾ of His creation.

celaleyn:148-148.t: ﴿لَا يُحِبُّ اللَّهُ الْجَهْرَ بِالسُّوءِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ﴾ from anyone, i.e. He punishes him for it ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ ظُلِمَ﴾ for He does not take him to task for saying it openly, by telling of the wrong of the one who wronged him and supplicating against him ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ سَمِيعًا﴾ of what is said ﴿عَلِيمًا﴾ of what is done

celaleyn:149-149.t: ﴿إِنْ تُبْدُوا﴾ display ﴿خَيْرًا﴾ of righteous deeds ﴿أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ﴾ do it secretly ﴿أَوْ تَعْفُوا عَنْ سُوءٍ﴾ a wrong ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَفُوًّا قَدِيرًا﴾

celaleyn:150-150.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْفُرُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَيُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يُفَرِّقُوا بَيْنَ اللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ﴾ by believing in Him but not in them ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ نُؤْمِنُ بِبَعْضٍ﴾ of the messengers ﴿وَنَكْفُرُ بِبَعْضٍ﴾ of them ﴿وَيُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَتَّخِذُوا بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ﴾ disbelief and faith ﴿سَبِيلًا﴾ a path which they take

celaleyn:151-151.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْكَافِرُونَ حَقًّا﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasising the content of the clause before it ﴿وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابًا مُهِينًا﴾ possessing humiliation; it is the punishment of the Fire

celaleyn:152-152.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ﴾ all of them ﴿وَلَمْ يُفَرِّقُوا بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ أُولَئِكَ سَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِمْ﴾ with nūn and with yāʾ [يُؤْتِيهِمْ] ﴿أُجُورَهُمْ﴾ the reward of their deeds ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا﴾ to His friends ﴿رَحِيمًا﴾ to the people of obedience to Him

celaleyn:153-153.t: ﴿يَسْأَلُكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Jews ﴿أَنْ تُنَزِّلَ [أَنْ تَنَزَّلَ] عَلَيْهِمْ كِتَابًا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ﴾ all at once, as it was sent down upon Moses — out of obstinacy; so if you find that grave ﴿فَقَدْ سَأَلُوا﴾ i.e. their forefathers ﴿مُوسَى أَكْبَرَ﴾ greater ﴿مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالُوا أَرِنَا اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً﴾ visibly ﴿فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ﴾ death, as a punishment for them ﴿بِظُلْمِهِمْ﴾ in that they were obstinate in asking ﴿ثُمَّ اتَّخَذُوا الْعِجْلَ﴾ as a god ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ﴾ the miracles [testifying] to the oneness of Allah ﴿فَعَفَوْنَا عَنْ ذَلِكَ﴾ and did not exterminate them ﴿وَآتَيْنَا مُوسَى سُلْطَانًا مُبِينًا﴾ clear, manifest authority over them, in that he commanded them to kill themselves as repentance, and they obeyed him

celaleyn:154-154.t: ﴿وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَهُمُ الطُّورَ﴾ the mountain ﴿بِمِيثَاقِهِمْ﴾ because of taking the covenant from them, so that they would fear, and they accepted it ﴿وَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ﴾ while it was overshadowing them ﴿ادْخُلُوا الْبَابَ﴾ the gate of the town ﴿سُجَّدًا﴾ a prostration of bowing ﴿وَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ لَا تَعْدُوا﴾ — and in one reading with fatḥa on the ʿayn and doubling of the dāl, in which there is assimilation (idghām) of the original tāʾ into the dāl, i.e. لَا تَعْتَدُوا ﴿فِي السَّبْتِ﴾ by catching fish on it ﴿وَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُمْ مِيثَاقًا غَلِيظًا﴾ on that, but they broke it.

celaleyn:155-155.t: ﴿فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ﴾ مَا is redundant (zāʾida), and the bāʾ is causal, attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted, i.e. "We cursed them because of their breaking" ﴿مِيثَاقَهُمْ وَكُفْرِهِمْ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَقَتْلِهِمُ الْأَنْبِيَاءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَقَوْلِهِمْ﴾ to the Prophet ﷺ ﴿قُلُوبُنَا غُلْفٌ﴾ they do not take in your words ﴿بَلْ طَبَعَ﴾ sealed ﴿اللَّهُ عَلَيْهَا بِكُفْرِهِمْ﴾ so they do not take in admonition ﴿فَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾ of them, like ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām and his companions

celaleyn:156-156.t: ﴿وَبِكُفْرِهِمْ﴾ a second time, in Jesus; the bāʾ is repeated to separate between it and what it is conjoined to ﴿وَقَوْلِهِمْ عَلَى مَرْيَمَ بُهْتَانًا عَظِيمًا﴾ in that they accused her of fornication

celaleyn:157-157.t: ﴿وَقَوْلِهِمْ﴾ boastfully ﴿إِنَّا قَتَلْنَا الْمَسِيحَ عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ﴾ as they claimed; i.e. for the sum of that We punished them. Allah the Exalted said, giving them the lie about killing him: ﴿وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ وَلَكِنْ شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ﴾ the one killed and crucified — who was their companion — was made to resemble Jesus, i.e. Allah cast his likeness upon him, so they thought he was him ﴿وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ﴾ i.e. about Jesus ﴿لَفِي شَكٍّ مِنْهُ﴾ about his killing, since some of them said, when they saw the one killed: "The face is the face of Jesus, but the body is not his body, so it is not him," while others said: "Rather, it is he" ﴿مَا لَهُمْ بِهِ﴾ of his killing ﴿مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِلَّا اتِّبَاعَ الظَّنِّ﴾ a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), i.e. but they follow in it the conjecture they imagined ﴿وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ يَقِينًا﴾ an emphatic ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida, emphasising circumstantial) for the negation of the killing

celaleyn:158-158.t: ﴿بَلْ رَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا﴾ in His dominion ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in His making

celaleyn:159-159.t: ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ not [مَا] ﴿مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ﴾ anyone ﴿إِلَّا لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ﴾ in Jesus ﴿قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ﴾ i.e. [the death of] the one of the People of the Book, when he sees the angels of death, so his faith will not benefit him; or before the death of Jesus, when he descends near the Hour, as has come in a hadith ﴿وَيَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ يَكُونُ﴾ Jesus ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيدًا﴾ to what they did when he was sent to them

celaleyn:160-160.t: ﴿فَبِظُلْمٍ﴾ i.e. because of wrongdoing ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ هَادُوا﴾ they are the Jews ﴿حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ طَيِّبَاتٍ أُحِلَّتْ لَهُمْ﴾ they are those in His saying, Exalted is He: {حَرَّمْنَا كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ} — the ayah ﴿وَبِصَدِّهِمْ﴾ people ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ His religion, a hindering ﴿كَثِيرًا﴾

celaleyn:161-161.t: ﴿وَأَخْذِهِمُ الرِّبَا وَقَدْ نُهُوا عَنْهُ﴾ in the Torah ﴿وَأَكْلِهِمْ أَمْوَالَ النَّاسِ بِالْبَاطِلِ﴾ through bribes in judgement ﴿وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ مِنْهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ painful

celaleyn:162-162.t: ﴿لَكِنِ الرَّاسِخُونَ﴾ the firmly established ﴿فِي الْعِلْمِ مِنْهُمْ﴾ like ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām ﴿وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ the Emigrants and the Helpers ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ﴾ of the Books ﴿وَالْمُقِيمِينَ الصَّلَوةَ﴾ accusative as praise (naṣb ʿalā al-madḥ), and it has been read in the nominative ﴿وَالْمُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَوةَ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ أُولَئِكَ سَنُؤْتِيهِمْ﴾ with nūn and with yāʾ ﴿أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾ it is Paradise.

celaleyn:163-163.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ كَمَا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى نُوحٍ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ﴾ ﴿وَ﴾ as [كَمَا] ﴿أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ﴾ his two sons ﴿وَيَعْقُوبَ﴾ son of Isaac ﴿وَالْأَسْبَاطِ﴾ his children ﴿وَعِيسَى وَأَيُّوبَ وَيُونُسَ وَهَارُونَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ وَآتَيْنَا﴾ his father ﴿دَاوُدَ زَبُورًا﴾ with fatḥa, a name for the Book given; and with ḍamma, a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of مَزْبُورًا, i.e. written

celaleyn:164-164.t: ﴿وَ﴾ We sent ﴿رُسُلًا قَدْ قَصَصْنَاهُمْ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَرُسُلًا لَمْ نَقْصُصْهُمْ عَلَيْكَ﴾ It is narrated that He, Exalted is He, sent eight thousand prophets: four thousand from the Children of Israel and four thousand from the rest of mankind; the Shaykh said this in Sūrat Ghāfir ﴿وَكَلَّمَ اللَّهُ مُوسَى﴾ without intermediary ﴿تَكْلِيمًا﴾

celaleyn:165-165.t: ﴿رُسُلًا﴾ a badal (substitute) of the رُسُلًا before it ﴿مُبَشِّرِينَ﴾ of reward to whoever believes ﴿وَمُنْذِرِينَ﴾ of punishment to whoever disbelieves. We sent them ﴿لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَى اللَّهِ حُجَّةٌ﴾ to be put forward ﴿بَعْدَ﴾ the sending of ﴿الرُّسُلِ﴾ to them, so that they would say: {رَبَّنَا لَوْلَا أَرْسَلْتَ إِلَيْنَا رَسُولًا فَنَتَّبِعَ آيَاتِكَ وَنَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ}; so We sent them to cut off their excuse ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا﴾ in His dominion ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in His making. And [the following] was revealed when the Jews were asked about his ﷺ prophethood and denied it

celaleyn:166-166.t: ﴿لَكِنِ اللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ﴾ makes clear your prophethood ﴿بِمَا أَنْزَلَ إِلَيْكَ﴾ of the inimitable Quran ﴿أَنْزَلَهُ﴾ bound up ﴿بِعِلْمِهِ﴾ i.e. knowing it, or with His knowledge in it ﴿وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ يَشْهَدُونَ﴾ for you as well ﴿وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا﴾ to that

celaleyn:167-167.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ in Allah ﴿وَصَدُّوا﴾ people ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ the religion of Islam, by concealing the description of Muhammad ﷺ — and they are the Jews ﴿قَدْ ضَلُّوا ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ from the truth

celaleyn:168-168.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ in Allah ﴿وَظَلَمُوا﴾ His Prophet, by concealing his description ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ طَرِيقًا﴾ of the paths

celaleyn:169-169.t: ﴿إِلَّا طَرِيقَ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ i.e. the path leading to it ﴿خَالِدِينَ﴾ destined for eternity ﴿فِيهَا﴾ when they enter it ﴿أَبَدًا وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرًا﴾ easy

celaleyn:170-170.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ﴾ i.e. people of Mecca ﴿قَدْ جَاءَكُمُ الرَّسُولُ﴾ Muhammad ﷺ ﴿بِالْحَقِّ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَآمِنُوا﴾ in him, and aim for ﴿خَيْرًا لَكُمْ﴾ than what you are in ﴿وَإِنْ تَكْفُرُوا﴾ in him ﴿فَإِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ as dominion, creation and servants, so your disbelief does not harm Him ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا﴾ of His creation ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in what He does with them

celaleyn:171-171.t: ﴿يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Gospel ﴿لَا تَغْلُوا﴾ go beyond the bound ﴿فِي دِينِكُمْ وَلَا تَقُولُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ إِلَّا﴾ the saying that is ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾ of declaring Him free of partner and child ﴿إِنَّمَا الْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ وَكَلِمَتُهُ أَلْقَاهَا﴾ Allah conveyed it ﴿إِلَى مَرْيَمَ وَرُوحٌ﴾ i.e. possessing a spirit ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ it is attributed to Him, Exalted is He, to honour him; and he is not, as you claimed, the son of Allah, or a god with Him, or the third of three, because the possessor of a spirit is composite, and God is free of compositeness and of having the composite attributed to Him ﴿فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَلَا تَقُولُوا﴾ the gods are ﴿ثَلَاثَةٌ﴾ Allah, Jesus and his mother ﴿انْتَهُوا﴾ from that, and bring ﴿خَيْرًا لَكُمْ﴾ than it — and it is the affirmation of [Allah's] oneness ﴿إِنَّمَا اللَّهُ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ سُبْحَانَهُ﴾ declaring Him free of [عَنْ] ﴿أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ as creation, dominion and servants, and being owned is incompatible with sonship ﴿وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا﴾ a witness to that

celaleyn:172-172.t: ﴿لَنْ يَسْتَنْكِفَ﴾ be too proud and disdainful ﴿الْمَسِيحُ﴾ whom you claimed to be a god, [too proud] to [عَنْ] ﴿أَنْ يَكُونَ عَبْدًا لِلَّهِ وَلَا الْمَلَائِكَةُ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ﴾ to Allah are too proud to be servants. This is one of the finest digressions (istiṭrād); it was mentioned to refute whoever claimed that they are gods or daughters of Allah, just as what precedes it refuted the Christians who claimed that, whom it is intended to address ﴿وَمَنْ يَسْتَنْكِفْ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِ وَيَسْتَكْبِرْ فَسَيَحْشُرُهُمْ إِلَيْهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ in the Hereafter

celaleyn:173-173.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ فَيُوَفِّيهِمْ أُجُورَهُمْ﴾ the reward of their deeds ﴿وَيَزِيدُهُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never occurred to the heart of a human being ﴿وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ اسْتَنْكَفُوا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾ from worshipping Him ﴿فَيُعَذِّبُهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ painful; it is the punishment of the Fire ﴿وَلَا يَجِدُونَ لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿وَلِيًّا﴾ who wards it off from them ﴿وَلَا نَصِيرًا﴾ who protects them from it

celaleyn:174-174.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ بُرْهَانٌ﴾ a proof ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ against you, and it is the Prophet ﷺ ﴿وَأَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكُمْ نُورًا مُبِينًا﴾ clear, and it is the Quran

celaleyn:175-175.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَاعْتَصَمُوا بِهِ فَسَيُدْخِلُهُمْ فِي رَحْمَةٍ مِنْهُ وَفَضْلٍ وَيَهْدِيهِمْ إِلَيْهِ صِرَاطًا﴾ a path ﴿مُسْتَقِيمًا﴾ it is the religion of Islam

celaleyn:176-176.t: ﴿يَسْتَفْتُونَكَ﴾ about kalāla ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِي الْكَلَالَةِ إِنِ امْرُؤٌ﴾ nominative by a verb which is explained by ﴿هَلَكَ﴾ died ﴿لَيْسَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ﴾ i.e. nor parent — and this is kalāla ﴿وَلَهُ أُخْتٌ﴾ of both parents or of the father ﴿فَلَهَا نِصْفُ مَا تَرَكَ وَهُوَ﴾ i.e. the brother, likewise ﴿يَرِثُهَا﴾ all that she left ﴿إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهَا وَلَدٌ﴾ but if she has a male child, he gets nothing; or a female, then he gets what remains of her share. And if the sister or the brother is from the mother, then his fixed share is a sixth, as preceded at the beginning of the sūra ﴿فَإِنْ كَانَتَا﴾ i.e. the sisters ﴿اثْنَتَيْنِ﴾ i.e. or more, because it was revealed about Jābir, who died leaving sisters ﴿فَلَهُمَا الثُّلُثَانِ مِمَّا تَرَكَ﴾ the brother ﴿وَإِنْ كَانُوا﴾ i.e. the heirs ﴿إِخْوَةً رِجَالًا وَنِسَاءً فَلِلذَّكَرِ﴾ of them ﴿مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ﴾ the laws of your religion, so [لِ] ﴿أَنْ﴾ not [لَا] ﴿تَضِلُّوا وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ including inheritance. The two Shaykhs [al-Bukhārī and Muslim] narrated from al-Barāʾ that it was the last ayah revealed, i.e. of [those on] the shares of inheritance. [Translator's note: Jābir was alive when the ayah was revealed — he was ill and had only sisters; the text's "who died" (وَقَدْ مَاتَ) is translated as written.]

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَرِثُوا النِّسَاءَ﴾ i.e. their persons ﴿كَرْهًا﴾ with fatḥa and ḍamma, two dialectal forms, i.e. compelling them to that. In the Jāhiliyya they used to inherit the wives of their relatives: if they wished they married them without a dowry, or married her off and took her dowry, or prevented her [Translator's note: from marrying] until she ransomed herself with what she had inherited or died and they inherited from her. So they were forbidden that ﴿وَلَا﴾ that ﴿تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ﴾ i.e. prevent your wives from marrying others by keeping them, while you have no desire for them, to harm them ﴿لِتَذْهَبُوا بِبَعْضِ مَا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ﴾ of the dowry ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ يَأْتِينَ بِفَاحِشَةٍ مُبَيَّنَةٍ﴾ with fatḥa and kasra on the yāʾ [مُبَيِّنَةٍ], i.e. made clear, or it is clear: i.e. fornication or recalcitrance (nushūz); then you may put pressure on them until they ransom themselves from you and seek khulʿ (divorce for compensation) ﴿وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ i.e. with graciousness in speech, maintenance and spending the night ﴿فَإِنْ كَرِهْتُمُوهُنَّ﴾ then be patient ﴿فَعَسَى أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئًا وَيَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ فِيهِ خَيْرًا كَثِيرًا﴾ and perhaps He will put that in them, by granting you a righteous child from them

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَإِنْ أَرَدْتُمُ اسْتِبْدَالَ زَوْجٍ مَكَانَ زَوْجٍ﴾ i.e. taking her in her place, by your having divorced her ﴿وَ﴾ having (qad) ﴿آتَيْتُمْ إِحْدَاهُنَّ﴾ i.e. the wives ﴿قِنْطَارًا﴾ much wealth as dowry ﴿فَلَا تَأْخُذُوا مِنْهُ شَيْئًا أَتَأْخُذُونَهُ بُهْتَانًا﴾ wrongfully ﴿وَإِثْمًا مُبِينًا﴾ clear. Their accusative is as ḥāl (circumstantial), and the interrogative is for rebuke and for denial

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَكَيْفَ تَأْخُذُونَهُ﴾ i.e. on what grounds ﴿وَقَدْ أَفْضَى﴾ has reached ﴿بَعْضُكُمْ إِلَى بَعْضٍ﴾ through intercourse, which establishes the dowry ﴿وَأَخَذْنَ مِنْكُمْ مِيثَاقًا﴾ a covenant ﴿غَلِيظًا﴾ firm, which is what Allah has commanded: retaining them in kindness or releasing them with excellence

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿وَلَا تَنْكِحُوا مَا﴾ in the sense of مَنْ ("whom") ﴿نَكَحَ آبَاؤُكُمْ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ إِلَّا﴾ but ﴿مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾ of your doing that, for it is pardoned ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ i.e. marrying them ﴿كَانَ فَاحِشَةً﴾ vile ﴿وَمَقْتًا﴾ a cause of loathing from Allah, which is the most intense hatred ﴿وَسَاءَ﴾ evil is ﴿سَبِيلًا﴾ as a way, that

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أُمَّهَاتُكُمْ﴾ to marry them; and it includes grandmothers on the father's or mother's side ﴿وَبَنَاتُكُمْ﴾ and it includes the daughters of children, however far down ﴿وَأَخَوَاتُكُمْ﴾ on the father's or mother's side ﴿وَعَمَّاتُكُمْ﴾ i.e. the sisters of your fathers and grandfathers ﴿وَخَالَاتُكُمْ﴾ i.e. the sisters of your mothers and grandmothers ﴿وَبَنَاتُ الْأَخِ وَبَنَاتُ الْأُخْتِ﴾ and their children are included in them ﴿وَأُمَّهَاتُكُمُ الَّتِي أَرْضَعْنَكُمْ﴾ before the completion of two years, five sucklings, as the hadith has made clear ﴿وَأَخَوَاتُكُمْ مِنَ الرَّضَاعَةِ﴾ and attached to that by the Sunna are the daughters through it, namely those whom the women he has had intercourse with suckled, and the paternal aunts, maternal aunts, brothers' daughters and sisters' daughters through it, because of the hadith: "Suckling makes unlawful what lineage makes unlawful." Narrated by al-Bukhārī and Muslim. ﴿وَأُمَّهَاتُ نِسَائِكُمْ وَرَبَائِبُكُمُ﴾ plural of رَبِيبَة, which is the wife's daughter by another man ﴿الَّتِي فِي حُجُورِكُمْ﴾ whom you raise; an adjective (ṣifa) in accord with what is usual, so it has no contrary implication (mafhūm) ﴿مِنْ نِسَائِكُمُ الَّتِي دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ﴾ i.e. with whom you have had intercourse ﴿فَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُونُوا دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ in marrying their daughters if you have separated from them ﴿وَحَلَائِلُ﴾ the wives of ﴿أَبْنَائِكُمُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ أَصْلَابِكُمْ﴾ unlike those you have adopted, whose wives you may marry ﴿وَأَنْ تَجْمَعُوا بَيْنَ الْأُخْتَيْنِ﴾ by lineage or suckling, in marriage; and attached to these by the Sunna is combining a woman with her paternal or maternal aunt. It is permitted to marry each one separately, and to own both together and have intercourse with one ﴿إِلَّا﴾ but ﴿مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾ in the Jāhiliyya, of their marrying some of those mentioned; there is no blame on you for it ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورًا﴾ for what you did before the prohibition ﴿رَحِيمًا﴾ to you in that.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿وَ﴾ forbidden to you are ﴿الْمُحْصَنَاتُ﴾ i.e. those who have husbands ﴿مِنَ النِّسَاءِ﴾ to marry them before they separate from their husbands, whether they are free Muslim women or not ﴿إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ﴾ of slave-women through capture: you may have intercourse with them, even if they have husbands in the abode of war, after establishing that the womb is free (istibrāʾ) ﴿كِتَابَ اللَّهِ﴾ accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. He has prescribed that ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَحَلَّ﴾ in the active and the passive [وَأُحِلَّ] ﴿لَكُمْ مَا وَرَاءَ ذَلِكُمْ﴾ i.e. other than the women forbidden to you ﴿أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا﴾ seek women ﴿بِأَمْوَالِكُمْ﴾ by dowry or price ﴿مُحْصِنِينَ﴾ marrying ﴿غَيْرَ مُسَافِحِينَ﴾ fornicating ﴿فَمَا﴾ whomever ﴿اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ﴾ enjoyed ﴿بِهِ مِنْهُنَّ﴾ of those you have married, through intercourse ﴿فَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾ their dowries which you assigned them ﴿فَرِيضَةً وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا تَرَاضَيْتُمْ﴾ you and they ﴿بِهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ الْفَرِيضَةِ﴾ of remitting it or part of it, or adding to it ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا﴾ of His creation ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in what He has arranged for them

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَمَنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنْكُمْ طَوْلًا﴾ i.e. means for ﴿أَنْ يَنْكِحَ الْمُحْصَنَاتِ﴾ the free women ﴿الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾ this follows what is usual, so it has no contrary implication (mafhūm) ﴿فَمِنْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ﴾ let him marry ﴿مِنْ فَتَيَاتِكُمُ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِإِيمَانِكُمْ﴾ so be content with its outward [Translator's note: form] and leave the inner secrets to Him, for He knows their details; and many a slave-woman surpasses the free woman in it. This is to make marrying slave-women feel acceptable ﴿بَعْضُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ﴾ i.e. you and they are equal in religion, so do not disdain marrying them ﴿فَانْكِحُوهُنَّ بِإِذْنِ أَهْلِهِنَّ﴾ their masters ﴿وَآتُوهُنَّ﴾ give them ﴿أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾ their dowries ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ without delay or reduction ﴿مُحْصَنَاتٍ﴾ chaste; a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿غَيْرَ مُسَافِحَاتٍ﴾ fornicating openly ﴿وَلَا مُتَّخِذَاتِ أَخْدَانٍ﴾ lovers who fornicate with them secretly ﴿فَإِذَا أُحْصِنَّ﴾ are given in marriage, and in one reading in the active: they marry ﴿فَإِنْ أَتَيْنَ بِفَاحِشَةٍ﴾ fornication ﴿فَعَلَيْهِنَّ نِصْفُ مَا عَلَى الْمُحْصَنَاتِ﴾ the free virgins, if they fornicate ﴿مِنَ الْعَذَابِ﴾ the ḥadd: so they are flogged fifty [Translator's note: lashes] and exiled for half a year, and male slaves are judged by analogy with them. Iḥṣān (married status) is not made a condition for the ḥadd being due, but rather to convey that there is no stoning for them at all ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. marrying slave-women when lacking means ﴿لِمَنْ خَشِيَ﴾ fears ﴿الْعَنَتَ﴾ fornication; its root meaning is hardship, and fornication is called by it because it is the cause of it, through the ḥadd in this world and punishment in the Hereafter ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ unlike the free man who does not fear it: it is not lawful for him to marry her; and likewise whoever has the means for a free woman; and this is the view of al-Shāfiʿī. Excluded by His saying {مِنْ فَتَيَاتِكُمُ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ} are the disbelieving women: it is not lawful for him to marry her even if he lacks means and fears ﴿وَأَنْ تَصْبِرُوا﴾ from marrying slave-women ﴿خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾ lest the child become a slave ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ by granting latitude in that

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ﴾ the laws of your religion and the interests of your affairs ﴿وَيَهْدِيَكُمْ سُنَنَ﴾ the ways of ﴿الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ of the prophets, in making lawful and unlawful, so that you follow them ﴿وَيَتُوبَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ bring you back from the disobedience to Him which you were in to obedience to Him ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ﴾ of you ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in what He has arranged for you.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ He repeated it in order to build upon it ﴿وَيُرِيدُ الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ الشَّهَوَاتِ﴾ the Jews and the Christians, or the Magians, or the fornicators ﴿أَنْ تَمِيلُوا مَيْلًا عَظِيمًا﴾ turn away from the truth by committing what is forbidden to you, so that you become like them

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُخَفِّفَ عَنْكُمْ﴾ make the rulings of the Sharia easy for you ﴿وَخُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ ضَعِيفًا﴾ unable to keep away from women and desires

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِالْبَاطِلِ﴾ by what is unlawful in the Sharia, such as usury and usurpation ﴿إِلَّا﴾ but ﴿أَنْ تَكُونَ﴾ occur ﴿تِجَارَةٌ﴾ and in one reading in the accusative [تِجَارَةً], i.e. the wealth is the wealth of trade, issuing ﴿عَنْ تَرَاضٍ مِنْكُمْ﴾ and with willingness, then you may consume it ﴿وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ by committing what leads to their destruction, whatever it may be, in this world or the Hereafter, as indicated by ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُمْ رَحِيمًا﴾ in His forbidding you that

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. what is forbidden ﴿عُدْوَانًا﴾ overstepping the lawful; a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿وَظُلْمًا﴾ a tawkīd (emphasis) ﴿فَسَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِ﴾ We will make him enter ﴿نَارًا﴾ in which he burns ﴿وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرًا﴾ easy

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿إِنْ تَجْتَنِبُوا كَبَائِرَ مَا تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ﴾ and they are those for which a threat has come, such as killing, fornication and theft; and from Ibn ʿAbbās: they are nearer to seven hundred ﴿نُكَفِّرْ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ﴾ the minor sins, through acts of obedience ﴿وَنُدْخِلْكُمْ مُدْخَلًا﴾ with ḍamma and fatḥa on the mīm, i.e. an entering or a place ﴿كَرِيمًا﴾ which is the Garden

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَلَا تَتَمَنَّوْا مَا فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ بِهِ بَعْضَكُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ﴾ in respect of this world or religion, lest it lead to mutual envy and hatred ﴿لِلرِّجَالِ نَصِيبٌ﴾ reward ﴿مِمَّا اكْتَسَبُوا﴾ because of what they did of jihad and other things ﴿وَلِلنِّسَاءِ نَصِيبٌ مِمَّا اكْتَسَبْنَ﴾ of obeying their husbands and guarding their chastity. It was revealed when Umm Salama said: "Would that we were men, so that we could fight in jihad and have the like of the men's reward." ﴿وَاسْأَلُوا﴾ with hamza and without it ﴿اللَّهَ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ what you need, He will give you ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمًا﴾ including the proper place of bounty and your asking

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿وَلِكُلٍّ﴾ of men and women ﴿جَعَلْنَا مَوَالِيَ﴾ agnatic heirs (ʿaṣaba) who are given ﴿مِمَّا تَرَكَ الْوَالِدَانِ وَالْأَقْرَبُونَ﴾ for them, of wealth ﴿وَالَّذِينَ عَاقَدَتْ﴾ with an alif and without it [عَقَدَتْ] ﴿أَيْمَانُكُمْ﴾ plural of يَمِين, in the sense of oath or hand, i.e. the confederates with whom you made a pact in the Jāhiliyya for support and inheritance ﴿فَآتُوهُمْ﴾ now ﴿نَصِيبَهُمْ﴾ their portions of the inheritance, which is a sixth ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدًا﴾ aware, including your state. This is abrogated by His saying {وَأُولُو الْأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَى بِبَعْضٍ} ("And those related by blood are more entitled to one another").

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿الرِّجَالُ قَوَّامُونَ﴾ in authority ﴿عَلَى النِّسَاءِ﴾ disciplining them and restraining them ﴿بِمَا فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ﴾ i.e. by His having preferred them over them in knowledge, intellect, guardianship and other things ﴿وَبِمَا أَنْفَقُوا﴾ on them ﴿مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ فَالصَّالِحَاتُ﴾ among them ﴿قَانِتَاتٌ﴾ obedient to their husbands ﴿حَافِظَاتٌ لِلْغَيْبِ﴾ i.e. guarding their chastity and other things in their husbands' absence ﴿بِمَا حَفِظَ﴾ them ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ in that He enjoined the husbands concerning them ﴿وَالَّتِي تَخَافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ﴾ their disobedience to you, its signs having appeared [Translator's note: the source text writes the Quranic word as وَالَّتِي; the muṣḥaf reads وَاللَّاتِي.] ﴿فَعِظُوهُنَّ﴾ make them fear Allah ﴿وَاهْجُرُوهُنَّ فِي الْمَضَاجِعِ﴾ withdraw to another bed if they show recalcitrance ﴿وَاضْرِبُوهُنَّ﴾ a non-injurious beating, if they do not return through the desertion ﴿فَإِنْ أَطَعْنَكُمْ﴾ in what is wanted from them ﴿فَلَا تَبْغُوا﴾ seek ﴿عَلَيْهِنَّ سَبِيلًا﴾ a way to beat them wrongfully ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيًّا كَبِيرًا﴾ so beware of Him punishing you if you wrong them

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ﴾ you know ﴿شِقَاقَ﴾ disagreement ﴿بَيْنِهِمَا﴾ between the spouses; the genitive construct (iḍāfa) is by extension (li-l-ittisāʿ), i.e. a discord between them ﴿فَابْعَثُوا﴾ to them, with their consent ﴿حَكَمًا﴾ an upright man ﴿مِنْ أَهْلِهِ﴾ his relatives ﴿وَحَكَمًا مِنْ أَهْلِهَا﴾ The husband appoints his arbiter as his agent for divorce and for accepting compensation for it, and she appoints her arbiter as her agent for khulʿ; they exert their effort and command the wrongdoer to return [Translator's note: to what is right], or separate them if they see fit. He the Exalted said: ﴿إِنْ يُرِيدَا﴾ i.e. the two arbiters ﴿إِصْلَاحًا يُوَفِّقِ اللَّهُ بَيْنَهُمَا﴾ between the spouses, i.e. He enables them to do what is obedience, whether reconciliation or separation ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا﴾ of everything ﴿خَبِيرًا﴾ of the inward as of the outward

daas-irab:139-140.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكافِرِينَ أَوْلِياءَ﴾ الذين is a relative noun in the position of the accusative (fī maḥall naṣb) as a naʿt (adjective) of المنافقين, or a badal (substitute); يتخذون is an imperfect verb, the wāw is its fāʿil (agent), and الكافرين is its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿أَوْلِياءَ﴾ is its second object, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ, being a sound masculine plural. ﴿أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ؟﴾ an imperfect verb, to which the adverb of place after it is attached; the wāw is its fāʿil and العزة is its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعاً﴾ inna and its noun; the Name of Majesty is genitive by the lām, and the two are attached to the omitted khabar (predicate); جميعا is a ḥāl, and the clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya). ﴿وَقَدْ نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتابِ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun عليكم, and likewise في الكتاب, are attached to the verb نزل, a past verb, passive [Translator's note: so in the source; نَزَّلَ as vocalized is active, with Allah as the implied agent]. ﴿أَنْ إِذا سَمِعْتُمْ آياتِ اللَّهِ﴾ أن is lightened from the heavy (anna), and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), i.e. أنه; إذا is an adverb for future time, and the clause after it is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿يُكْفَرُ بِها﴾ an imperfect verb, passive (mabnī li-l-majhūl), and the preposition and its genitive noun take the place of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and likewise ﴿وَيُسْتَهْزَأُ بِها﴾. ﴿فَلا تَقْعُدُوا مَعَهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lā of prohibition, to which the adverb of place معهم is attached; the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿حَتَّى يَخُوضُوا فِي حَدِيثٍ غَيْرِهِ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى, to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached; the wāw is its fāʿil, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the genitive by حتى, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb تقعدوا before them; غيره is a naʿt. ﴿إِنَّكُمْ إِذاً مِثْلُهُمْ﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar; إذن is a particle of answer and requital that has no governing effect, and the clause gives the reason. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ جامِعُ الْمُنافِقِينَ﴾ inna, its noun, its khabar and a muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْكافِرِينَ﴾ conjoined (ʿaṭf). ﴿فِي جَهَنَّمَ﴾ the two are attached to جامع. ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾ a ḥāl, and the clause also gives the reason.

daas-irab:141-141.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَرَبَّصُونَ بِكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the relative noun is also a naʿt (adjective) of المنافقين, and the clause after it is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فَإِنْ كانَ لَكُمْ فَتْحٌ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun لكم are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of كان, which is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and فتح is its noun. ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted naʿt of فتح. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) not joined to the fāʾ or to the إذا of surprise. ﴿أَلَمْ نَكُنْ مَعَكُمْ؟﴾ the adverb of place is attached to an omitted khabar of نكن, whose noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "نحن"; the hamza is for interrogation, and the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿وَإِنْ كانَ لِلْكافِرِينَ نَصِيبٌ قالُوا﴾ like ﴿فَإِنْ كانَ لَكُمْ فَتْحٌ﴾. ﴿أَلَمْ نَسْتَحْوِذْ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb before them, and the clause is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَنَمْنَعْكُمْ﴾ conjoined to نستحوذ. ﴿مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ the two are attached to the verb before them. ﴿فَاللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ﴾ the two adverbs بينكم and يوم are attached to the verb يحكم, and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) الله; the clause ﴿فَاللَّهُ﴾ is resumptive; القيامة is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَلَنْ يَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ لِلْكافِرِينَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ سَبِيلًا﴾ للكافرين: the two are attached to يجعل and they are the first object, and سبيلا is the second object; على المؤمنين: the two are attached to the verb or to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from سبيلا; and the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:142-143.t:
﴿إِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ يُخادِعُونَ اللَّهَ﴾
inna and its noun, and the verbal clause after it is its khabar (predicate). ﴿وَهُوَ خادِعُهُمْ﴾
a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَإِذا قامُوا إِلَى الصَّلاةِ قامُوا كُسالى﴾
the first clause قاموا is in the position of the genitive by annexation because it follows إذا, and the second clause قاموا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussivizing condition; كسالى is a ḥāl, accusative (manṣūb) with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa. ﴿يُراؤُنَ النَّاسَ﴾
an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿وَلا يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾
conjoined to what precedes it; قليلا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and إلا is a particle of restriction. ﴿مُذَبْذَبِينَ﴾
a ḥāl, accusative with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural, and the adverb ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ after it is attached to it, and the demonstrative ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿لا إِلى هؤُلاءِ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "not inclining to these". ﴿وَلا إِلى هؤُلاءِ﴾ conjoined. ﴿وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ﴾ من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ, and [يضلل is] the jussive protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil and its object is omitted, i.e. "whomever Allah leads astray (يضلله)"; and the clause ﴿فَلَنْ تَجِدَ﴾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. ﴿لَهُ سَبِيلًا﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl of سبيلا, and the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من.

daas-irab:144-144.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿لا تَتَّخِذُوا الْكافِرِينَ أَوْلِياءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lā of prohibition, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); الكافرين is its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and أولياء its second; من دون: the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of أولياء; المؤمنين is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with the yāʾ. ﴿أَتُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَجْعَلُوا لِلَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ سُلْطاناً﴾ أن and the verb after it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of the verb تريدون, and the wāw is the fāʿil; لله: the two are attached to the verb تجعلوا and they are the first object, and سلطانا is the second object; عليكم: the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of ﴿سُلْطاناً﴾. ﴿مُبِيناً﴾ a naʿt. The clause ﴿لا تَتَّخِذُوا﴾ is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and the clause ﴿أَتُرِيدُونَ﴾ is resumptive.

daas-irab:145-146.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ فِي الدَّرْكِ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of inna; المنافقين is its noun. ﴿الْأَسْفَلِ﴾ a naʿt (adjective). ﴿مِنَ النَّارِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from الدرك. ﴿وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُمْ نَصِيراً﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تجد and they are the first object, and نصيرا is the second object; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تابُوا﴾ الذين is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative by exception after إلا, and the clause تابوا is its ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَأَصْلَحُوا وَاعْتَصَمُوا بِاللَّهِ، وَأَخْلَصُوا دِينَهُمْ لِلَّهِ﴾ all of these are conjoined [Translator's note: the source has the typo كسل for كل]. ﴿فَأُولئِكَ مَعَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the adverb of place مع is attached to its omitted khabar; المؤمنين is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَسَوْفَ يُؤْتِ اللَّهُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَجْراً عَظِيماً﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its two objects, and عظيما is a naʿt.

daas-irab:147-147.t: ﴿ما يَفْعَلُ اللَّهُ بِعَذابِكُمْ﴾ ما is an interrogative noun; [يفعل is] an imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and its fāʿil (agent) [is the Name of Majesty]; the interrogative noun before it is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿إِنْ شَكَرْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and it is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it: "If you are grateful and believe, then what would Allah do with your punishment?". ﴿وَآمَنْتُمْ﴾ conjoined. ﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿شاكِراً عَلِيماً﴾ khabar (predicate) of kāna.

daas-irab:37-37.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ﴾: (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ), as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هم الذين". It has also been said to be a badal (substitute) for (من كان); it has also been said to be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted; or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb: "أذم الذين" (I blame those who…). The clause (يبخلون) is its ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَيَأْمُرُونَ النَّاسَ بِالْبُخْلِ﴾: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) it. ﴿وَيَكْتُمُونَ ما﴾: an imperfect verb; the wāw is its fāʿil and the relative noun is its mafʿūl bihi. The two clauses are maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿آتاهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾: a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the Name of Majesty (Allah) is its fāʿil. ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾: attached to (آتاهم), or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted second object. ﴿وَأَعْتَدْنا لِلْكافِرِينَ عَذاباً مُهِيناً﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; (نا) is its fāʿil, (عذابا) its mafʿūl bihi, and (مهينا) a naʿt (adjective). The clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:38-39.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ﴾: the relative noun is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to what precedes it; the clause after it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿أَمْوالَهُمْ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿رِئاءَ﴾: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿النَّاسِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَلا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ﴾: the clause is maʿṭūf to what precedes it; (لا) is negating and has no governing effect. ﴿وَلا بِالْيَوْمِ﴾: conjoined to (الله). ﴿الْآخِرِ﴾: naʿt (adjective). ﴿وَمَنْ يَكُنِ الشَّيْطانُ﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb and its noun (ism); (من) is a jussive conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (يكن) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿قَرِيناً﴾: its khabar (predicate). ﴿لَهُ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of (قرينا), or to (قرينا). ﴿فَساءَ قَرِيناً﴾: a rigid (jāmid) past verb expressing blame; (قرينا) is a tamyīz (specification), and the one specifically blamed is omitted, the implied form being: "فساء الشيطان قرينا" (an evil companion is Satan). The clause is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من). ﴿وَماذا عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: (ماذا) is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; (عليهم) is attached to an omitted khabar. It is also permissible for (ما) to be an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ and (ذا) a relative noun as its khabar, with the preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ṣila. ﴿لَوْ آمَنُوا﴾: (لو) is a conditional particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil; it is in the position of the jussive as the protasis, and the apodosis is omitted, the implied form being: "لو آمنوا فماذا عليهم". [Translator's note: the source says the verb is "in the position of the jussive" although لو is normally a non-jussive conditional particle; translated as written.] ﴿بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ﴾: attached to the verb (آمنوا). ﴿وَأَنْفَقُوا﴾: conjoined to (آمنوا). ﴿مِمَّا رَزَقَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾: a past verb, a mafʿūl bihi and a fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. The preposition and its genitive noun (مما) are attached to (أنفقوا). ﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ بِهِمْ عَلِيماً﴾: (كان), its noun and its khabar; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the khabar (عليما). The clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:40-42.t:
﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: (إن), and the Name of Majesty is its noun (ism). ﴿لا يَظْلِمُ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ﴾: (لا) is negating, and an imperfect verb; (مثقال) is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), the implied form being: "لا يظلم ظلما مثقال". It has also been said to be a second object, the first object being omitted, i.e. "لا يظلم أحدا مثقال". The clause is the khabar (predicate) of (إن), and (ذرة) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَإِنْ تَكُ﴾: (إن) is conditional, and a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) with an implied (muqaddar) sukūn on the nūn, which was omitted for lightness, just as the wāw was omitted to prevent the meeting of two quiescent letters. Its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو". ﴿حَسَنَةً﴾: its khabar. The clause (وإن تك) is resumptive. ﴿يُضاعِفْها﴾: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), jussive; the hāʾ is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a condition not joined with the fāʾ. ﴿وَيُؤْتِ مِنْ لَدُنْهُ﴾: (لدنه) is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of the genitive (majrūr) by (من); the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يؤت). The clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿أَجْراً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَظِيماً﴾: naʿt.
﴿فَكَيْفَ﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied form being: "فكيف يصنعون ...؟" (how then will they act?); or in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as a khabar, the implied form being: "كيف حالهم" (how will their state be?). ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb for future time, attached to the omitted verb or the omitted mubtadaʾ. ﴿جِئْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (جئنا); (أمة) is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِشَهِيدٍ﴾: also attached to the verb. ﴿وَجِئْنا بِكَ﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (جئنا). ﴿عَلى هؤُلاءِ﴾: attached to the ḥāl (شهيدا); the clause is maʿṭūf. ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: (يوم) is a mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), an adverb of time attached to (يود); (إذ) is an adverb for past time, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of the genitive by annexation, and the tanwīn and the adverb [Translator's note: so in the source; normally it is the tanwīn alone that is said to compensate] compensate for the omitted clause, the implied form being: "يوم إذ جئنا يود الذين". ﴿يَوَدُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, and the relative noun is its fāʿil; the clause after it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the clause (يود) is resumptive. ﴿وَعَصَوُا الرَّسُولَ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the clause is maʿṭūf. ﴿لَوْ تُسَوَّى بِهِمُ الْأَرْضُ﴾: a passive imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (لو) is a maṣdar-forming particle, which together with the verb after it is interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, i.e. "تسوية" (being levelled). ﴿وَلا يَكْتُمُونَ اللَّهَ حَدِيثاً﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil, (الله), the Name of Majesty, is its first object and (حديثا) its second object. The clause is maʿṭūf to the clause ﴿يَوَدُّ﴾.

daas-irab:43-43.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: its i'rab has preceded. ﴿لا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلاةَ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive (lā al-nāhiya), the sign of its jussive being the omission of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). The clause is resumptive. ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ سُكارى﴾: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the wāw is the wāw of the ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause is circumstantial. ﴿حَتَّى تَعْلَمُوا ما تَقُولُونَ﴾: the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied (muḍmara) (أن) after (حتى) and the verb (تعلموا) is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) by the preposition; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تقربوا). The relative noun is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause (تقولون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَلا جُنُباً﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (جنبا) is a ḥāl, the implied form being "ولا تصلوا جنبا" (and do not pray while in a state of major impurity) or "لا تقربوا مواضع الصلاة جنبا" (do not approach the places of prayer in a state of major impurity); (لا) is negating. ﴿إِلَّا عابِرِي سَبِيلٍ﴾: (إلا) is a particle of exception; (عابري) is the excepted, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. It has also been said that (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) and (عابري) is a ḥāl. ﴿حَتَّى تَغْتَسِلُوا﴾: like (حتى تعلموا); the interpreted maṣdar is genitive by (حتى), and the two are attached to (لا تقربوا). ﴿وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ مَرْضى﴾: (كان), its noun and its khabar; the clause of (كان) is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَوْ عَلى سَفَرٍ﴾: conjoined to (مرضى). ﴿أَوْ جاءَ أَحَدٌ مِنْكُمْ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (أحد). The clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿مِنَ الْغائِطِ﴾: attached to (جاء). ﴿أَوْ لامَسْتُمُ النِّساءَ﴾: likewise conjoined. ﴿فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا ماءً﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive, with its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is maʿṭūf to (كنتم). ﴿فَتَيَمَّمُوا صَعِيداً﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), because it is joined with the fāʾ. ﴿طَيِّباً﴾: naʿt. ﴿فَامْسَحُوا بِوُجُوهِكُمْ﴾: an imperative verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached; the wāw is its fāʿil. The clause is maʿṭūf to (تيمموا). It has also been said that the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿وَأَيْدِيكُمْ﴾: maʿṭūf, genitive with an implied (muqaddar) kasra. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: (إن), and the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿كانَ عَفُوًّا﴾: (كان) and its khabar; its noun is omitted. [Translator's note: so in the source; the noun of كان is usually described as a latent pronoun.] ﴿غَفُوراً﴾: a second khabar.

daas-irab:44-45.t:
﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, (لم) is jussive, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the omission of the weak letter because it is weak-final. ﴿إِلَى الَّذِينَ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تر). ﴿أُوتُوا نَصِيباً مِنَ الْكِتابِ﴾: a passive past verb; the wāw is its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and it is the first object, and (نصيبا) is the second object. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (نصيبا). The clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
﴿يَشْتَرُونَ الضَّلالَةَ﴾: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause is a mafʿūl bihi, considering (تر) to be a verb of the heart (cognition), not of sight.
﴿وَيُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَضِلُّوا﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar, "الضلالة" (going astray), is the mafʿūl bihi. ﴿السَّبِيلَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi of (تضلوا). The clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to what precedes it. ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِأَعْدائِكُمْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, ﴿أَعْلَمُ﴾. The clause is resumptive. ﴿وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ وَلِيًّا﴾: the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (الله), the Name of Majesty, is the fāʿil of (كفى); (وليا) is a tamyīz (specification). The clause is resumptive. ﴿وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ نَصِيراً﴾: conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:46-46.t: ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause ﴿هادُوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the clause ﴿يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of the omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "من الذين هادوا قوم يحرفون" (among those who are Jews are a people who distort). ﴿عَنْ مَواضِعِهِ﴾: attached to (يحرفون). ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ سَمِعْنا وَعَصَيْنا﴾: (ويقولون) is conjoined to (يحرفون); (سمعنا) is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿وَعَصَيْنا﴾: conjoined; the two clauses are the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَاسْمَعْ﴾: a verb of supplication; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (سمعنا). ﴿غَيْرَ﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative. ﴿مُسْمَعٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَراعِنا﴾: an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the weak letter; the fāʿil is "أنت" (you), and (نا) is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause is maʿṭūf to (اسمع). ﴿لَيًّا﴾: a ḥāl, accusative; it has also been said to be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿بِأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ﴾: attached to (ليا). ﴿وَطَعْناً﴾: maʿṭūf to (ليا); the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached to it. ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ﴾: (لو) is a conditional particle and the wāw is resumptive; (أن) and its noun, and the clause ﴿قالُوا﴾ is its khabar. (أن) and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of an omitted verb, the implied form being: "لو ثبت قولهم" (had their saying been established). ﴿سَمِعْنا وَأَطَعْنا﴾: like (سمعنا وعصينا). ﴿وَاسْمَعْ﴾: like the preceding one. ﴿وَانْظُرْنا﴾: conjoined to (اسمع). ﴿لَكانَ خَيْراً لَهُمْ﴾: (كان) and its khabar, to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو". The clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿وَأَقْوَمَ﴾: conjoined to (خيرا). ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾: a particle of rectification (istidrāk), and the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾: a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil. ﴿بِكُفْرِهِمْ﴾: attached to (لعنهم); the clause is maʿṭūf. ﴿فَلا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; (لا) is negating and the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾: the excepted, accusative with the fatḥa, and (إلا) is a particle of exception. It has also been said to be a naʿt of a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), with (إلا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), i.e. "لا يؤمنون إلا إيمانا قليلا" (they do not believe except with a little belief).

daas-irab:47-47.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ﴾: its i'rab has preceded. ﴿أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ﴾: a passive past verb and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and (الكتاب) is its object. ﴿آمِنُوا﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn, and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿بِما نَزَّلْنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (آمنوا); the clause ﴿نَزَّلْنا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿مُصَدِّقاً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لِما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (مصدقا). ﴿مَعَكُمْ﴾: an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila, i.e. "للذي وجد معكم" (to what is found with you). ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ﴾: attached to (آمنوا). ﴿أَنْ نَطْمِسَ﴾: the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وُجُوهاً﴾: the object of (نطمس). ﴿فَنَرُدَّها﴾: conjoined to (نطمس); the hāʾ is its object. ﴿عَلى أَدْبارِها﴾: attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "نردها ناكصة" (We turn them back reversed). ﴿أَوْ نَلْعَنَهُمْ﴾: conjoined to (نردها). ﴿كَما لَعَنَّا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; (ما) is maṣdar-forming, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the genitive by the kāf. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: "نلعنهم لعنا كلعننا أصحاب السبت" (We curse them with a cursing like Our cursing of the people of the Sabbath). ﴿أَصْحابَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿السَّبْتِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause is resumptive. ﴿وَكانَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ مَفْعُولًا﴾: (كان) and its noun, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi; (مفعولا) is its khabar (predicate). The clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined).

daas-irab:48-50.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ﴾: the interpreted maṣdar formed from the passive, accusative imperfect verb (يشرك) and the subjunctive-governing (أن) is in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb (يغفر).
