(أن يقاتلوكم) is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e.: from fighting you, and the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (حصرت). You may also make the interpreted maṣdar a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). (أو يقاتلوا قومهم) is conjoined to (يقاتلوكم), and (قومهم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ لَسَلَّطَهُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ) The wāw is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, brought to except this last group from the ruling of seizing and killing, and to include them among those under covenant. (لو) is conditional, and (شاء الله) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the lām connects the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis), and the clause (لسلطهم عليكم) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (فَلَقاتَلُوكُمْ فَإِنِ اعْتَزَلُوكُمْ فَلَمْ يُقاتِلُوكُمْ) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and (لقاتلوكم) is conjoined to (سلطكم) [Translator's note: so in the source, i.e. سلطهم], so it serves as a tawkīd (emphasis) of the apodosis, or as a badal (substitute) from the first.
A discussion of this lām will come in the section of Benefits. (فإن): the fāʾ is resumptive and (إن) conditional; (اعتزلوكم) is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, in the position of the jussive as the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis); the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (لم يقاتلوكم) is conjoined to (اعتزلوكم). (وَأَلْقَوْا إِلَيْكُمُ السَّلَمَ) is likewise conjoined. (فَما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ سَبِيلًا) The fāʾ connects the apodosis and (ما) is negating; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. (جعل) is a past verb that puts two objects in the accusative; (الله) is the fāʿil; (لكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted first mafʿūl bihi; (عليهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; and (سبيلا) is the second mafʿūl bihi.

* Benefits:
Ibn Hishām spoke about this verse and produced something delightful, saying: As for His saying: «أو جاءوكم حصرت صدورهم», the majority held that «حصرت صدورهم» is an informative (khabariyya) clause. Then they differed. A group, among them al-Akhfash, said:
it is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «جاء» with «قد» implied. Know that implying «قد» is obligatory according to the Basrans: they say that when a past-tense clause occurs as a ḥāl it must be joined with qad, either overt or implied (muqaddar). As for al-Akhfash, he does not consider it obligatory with the past verb when it occurs as a ḥāl; he says that the past-tense clause occurs as a ḥāl and is joined with «قد» if it is present, and if it is not present it needs no implied form.
This is supported by the reading of al-Ḥasan: «حصرة صدورهم», i.e. in the state of their being ḥaṣira, that is, constricted. Others said: it is an adjective, and so needs no implying of «قد».
Then these differed. It was said: the thing described is an omitted accusative, i.e.: "a people (qawman) whose breasts are constricted"; they held that implying a noun is easier than implying a particle.
And it was said: it is a mentioned genitive, namely «قوم» mentioned earlier, so there is no implying at all, and what lies between them is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ). This is supported by the fact that it was read with «أو» dropped; on that basis «جاءوكم» is an adjective of (قوم) and «حصرت» is a second adjective.
And it was said: it is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from «جاءوكم», because the coming includes the constriction; but this is far-fetched, because the constriction is an attribute of those coming.
Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Mubarrad said: the clause is performative (inshāʾiyya), its meaning being a supplication, like "may their hands be fettered", so it is resumptive. This was rejected on the ground that praying against them that their hearts be too constricted to fight their own people is not sound. It was answered that what is meant is praying against them that they be deprived of the capacity to fight altogether, in contempt of them.

A discussion of the lām in «ولقاتلوكم»:
Ibn ʿAṭiyya named this lām "the lām of correspondence and pairing" (lām al-muḥādhāh wa-l-izdiwāj), because it is in the position of the first; had there been no first, you would say: لقاتلوكم [Translator's note: so in the source; the intended form is presumably قاتلوكم without the lām]. Abū Ḥayyān said in comment on that: «Calling this lām the lām of correspondence and pairing is a strange naming; I have not seen it except in the expression of this man and the expression of Makkī before him.»

Comment on this discussion:
I say: there is no benefit beneath this discussion, which leads the student astray and avails nothing. I have pointed to this in the section of I'rab: it is no more than an emphasis of the apodosis, so it belongs to the category of repetition and substitution. We have only cited it for familiarisation, and so that the student may be safe from being deceived by the misleading name when he comes across it in their i'rab.

dervis-irab:91-91.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أُرْكِسُوا فِيها): they were overturned in it in the worst way. It has already been mentioned.
(ثَقِفْتُمُوهُمْ): thaqifa al-shayʾa thaqfan, of the pattern taʿiba: he took it. Thaqiftu al-rajula fī al-ḥarb: I caught up with the man in war; thaqiftuhu: I overcame him; thaqiftu al-ḥadītha:
I understood the speech quickly. Al-tathqīf originally means straightening crooked spears and reeds and making them even. From this meaning arose tathqīf al-ghulām, i.e. refining the boy and straightening his conduct; then al-thaqf came to mean caution and quickness of understanding. Finally the meaning was renewed in our age and became specific to learning and culture (al-thaqāfa) in knowledge. On this basis we observe the development of the language in every Arab country, just as the sons of every generation in every land of mankind have seen how their language rose with their rise and declined with their decline.

The living development of language:
Thus there is no social event or scientific or political awakening that is not accompanied by a development in the language or in meanings or in both together — we mean in the creation of new words for certain meanings, or the creation of new meanings for certain words, or in all of that. No one acquainted with the history of the Arabs and their literature is unaware of the linguistic revolution that Islam, for example, brought about alongside the religious, social and intellectual revolution.
Living examples of this living development will come to us in this wondrous Book.
From this starting point the necessity of this book for our developing youth becomes clear, so that in its light they may see the secrets of what they gather, and by its glow perceive the meaning of movement in the minds of those who went before; thereby the linguistic mind continues on the path of developing movement instead of stagnating in the stillness of material that was once among the products of the moving linguistic mind.

* I'rab:
(سَتَجِدُونَ آخَرِينَ يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَأْمَنُوكُمْ) A resumptive statement brought to establish the state of another group of the hypocrites, other than those alluded to before. The sīn is for continuous future; a delightful discussion of it will come in the section of Benefits.
(تجدون) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); (آخرين) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause (يريدون) is an adjective of (آخرين); (أن) and what falls within its scope form an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) that is the object of (يريدون). (وَيَأْمَنُوا قَوْمَهُمْ) is conjoined to what precedes. (كُلَّما رُدُّوا إِلَى الْفِتْنَةِ أُرْكِسُوا فِيها) (كلما) is an adverb of time containing the meaning of condition; its i'rab has already been given. The clause (ردوا إلى الفتنة) is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa), or has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī); the wāw is a nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The clause (أركسوا فيها) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, and (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أركسوا). (فَإِنْ لَمْ يَعْتَزِلُوكُمْ وَيُلْقُوا إِلَيْكُمُ السَّلَمَ) The fāʾ is resumptive and (إن) conditional; (لم) is a particle of negation, of conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning] and of the jussive; (يعتزلوكم) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم), and it is in the position of the jussive as the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis); (ويلقوا إليكم السلم) is conjoined to it. (فَخُذُوهُمْ وَاقْتُلُوهُمْ حَيْثُ ثَقِفْتُمُوهُمْ) The fāʾ connects the apodosis, and the clause (خذوهم) is in the position of the jussive as the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis); (اقتلوهم) is conjoined to (خذوهم); (حيث) is an adverb of place, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, attached to (اقتلوهم), and the clause (ثقفتموهم) is in the position of the genitive by annexation. (وَأُولئِكُمْ جَعَلْنا لَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطاناً مُبِيناً) The wāw is a conjunction; (أولئكم) is a demonstrative, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (جعلنا) is a khabar (predicate); (لكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of the accusative as the first mafʿūl bihi; (عليهم) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (سلطانا) is the second mafʿūl bihi and (مبينا) an adjective.

* Benefits:
An important discussion of the sīn:
The sīn is a particle that enters upon the imperfect verb and makes it purely future and continuous. The sīn was brought here as an indication that their trifling with the believers is a continuing matter, even though it had taken place in the past. That is because men of the disbelievers, when they came to Medina, would embrace Islam so that [the Muslims] would not fight them, and when they came to their own people they would disbelieve.
So the Lord, Glorified and Exalted, brought the sīn as an indication that this state of theirs is a continuing habit of theirs and that they had not abandoned it, even though it had occurred in the past.
Ibn Hishām claimed that the continuity is derived only from the imperfect verb, just as you say:
"So-and-so entertains guests and does good deeds", meaning that this is his custom; and that the sīn conveys the future, since continuity can only be in the future. Al-Zamakhsharī claimed that when it enters upon a verb that is loved or disliked, it conveys that it will occur without fail; and I have not seen anyone who understood the reasoning for that. Its reasoning is that it conveys the promise of the verb's occurrence, so its entering upon what conveys a promise or a threat requires emphasising it and confirming its meaning, because it is information upon information, and the object [of both] is one.

dervis-irab:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(لِلرِّجالِ نَصِيبٌ مِمَّا تَرَكَ الْوالِدانِ وَالْأَقْرَبُونَ): resumptive speech introduced to refute the practice of the Jāhiliyya of not giving inheritance to women and young children. للرجال is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); نصيب is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); مما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of نصيب; the clause ترك الوالدان is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; الأقربون is conjoined to الوالدان. (وَلِلنِّساءِ نَصِيبٌ مِمَّا تَرَكَ الْوالِدانِ وَالْأَقْرَبُونَ): conjoined to what preceded. (مِمَّا قَلَّ مِنْهُ أَوْ كَثُرَ نَصِيباً مَفْرُوضاً): the preposition and its genitive noun are a badal (substitute) of the preceding «مما»; the clause is the ṣila; منه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قلّ; أو كثر is conjoined to قلّ. نصيبا مفروضا may be parsed as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it stands in its place, the implied sense being "a giving"; it may also be parsed as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «قلّ», i.e. of what he left, little or much. Al-Zamakhsharī chose to make it accusative by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ) through an omitted verb meaning "I mean a share", but there is no need for that.

dervis-irab:8-9.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا حَضَرَ الْقِسْمَةَ أُولُوا الْقُرْبى وَالْيَتامى وَالْمَساكِينُ): the واو is resumptive; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition; the clause حضر القسمة is in the position of genitive by annexation; القسمة is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); أولو القربى is the fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the واو because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural; اليتامى and المساكين are conjoined to أولو القربى. (فَارْزُقُوهُمْ مِنْهُ وَقُولُوا لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفاً): the فاء links the apodosis of إذا; ارزقوهم is an imperative verb, its agent and its direct object; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussivising condition; منه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) قولوا [Translator's note: so in the source; منه evidently belongs with ارزقوهم]; قولا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and معروفا an adjective. (وَلْيَخْشَ الَّذِينَ لَوْ تَرَكُوا مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعافاً): the واو is a conjunction; the lām is the lām of command; يخش is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām; الذين is a relative noun, the fāʿil; لو is conditional; تركوا is a verb with its agent; من خلفهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تركوا; ذرية is a mafʿūl bihi and ضعافا an adjective. (خافُوا عَلَيْهِمْ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussivising condition; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خافوا; the object of خافوا is omitted, its implied form being "being lost and wandering"; more on it will come in the section of Rhetoric. (فَلْيَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ): the فاء is causal, because fearing [Allah] (التقوى) is caused by the fear which is dread; the lām is the lām of command; يتقوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by the lām; the واو is the fāʿil and الله the mafʿūl bihi. (وَلْيَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيداً): the clause is conjoined to فليتقوا; قولا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq and سديدا an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse there is the device of ījāz bi-l-ḥadhf (concision by omission), here in the omission of the object of خافوا, so that the mind may go every way in supplying it, and may display ingenuity in picturing the fear of the inevitable fate to which the affair of the weak ones comes in this life. You may supply it with the like of being lost, wandering, and being scattered in the paths of life and its branching ways, without a guardian to take care of them or a manager to manage their affairs. The poet glanced at the sky of this meaning in his delightful saying, excusing himself for fear and for staying behind, giving his daughters as the reason:
لقد زاد الحياة إليّ حبا ... بناتي إنهنّ من الضعاف
أحاذر أن يرين البؤس بعدي ... وأن يشربن رنقا غير صاف
وأن يعرين إن كسي الجواري ... فتنبو العين عن كرم عجاف
ولولاهن قد سوّيت مهري ... وفي الرحمن للضعفاء كاف
(My daughters have made life dearer to me, for they are among the weak. I fear they will see misery after me, and drink turbid, unclear water, and go naked when other girls are clothed, so that the eye turns away from noble [girls] grown lean. Were it not for them I would have saddled my colt — and in the Most Merciful there is sufficiency for the weak.)
Moreover, the omission of the direct object from speech has subtleties and wonders, as in our saying: "So-and-so loosens and binds, ratifies and annuls, harms and benefits." The basis in that is establishing the meaning intended in the mind for the thing absolutely.

* Benefits:
The view of the author of al-Mughnī and a discussion of it:
There has been much disagreement about this «لو». We shall cite the view of the author of al-Mughnī on the i'rab of this verse, then discuss it; that is not without enjoyment and benefit. He said: «The second category of «لو» is that it be a particle of condition in the future, except that it does not make jussive, as in the saying of Tawba ibn al-Ḥumayyir about Laylā al-Akhyaliyya:
ولو أن ليلى الأخيلية سلّمت ... عليّ ودوني جندل وصفائح
لسلّمت تسليم البشاشة أو زقا ... إليها صدى من جانب الأرض صائح
(If Laylā al-Akhyaliyya were to greet me while rocks and slabs lie over me, I would return the greeting of cheerfulness, or an owl-spirit would cry out to her from a side of the earth.)
and the words of the Exalted: «وليخش الذين ...» the verse; i.e. let those fear who, if they were on the verge of and close to leaving... We have interpreted leaving as being on the verge of leaving only because the address is to the guardians [of the will], and it is directed to them only before leaving, because after it they are dead.» This is what he said in al-Mughnī. The interpretation mentioned is not restricted to the address being to the guardians; rather it holds even if we say it is to the heirs or to those sitting with the sick man as well. In that case the mention of the guardians is not for exclusion but is limiting oneself to one of the meanings. The author of al-Kashshāf indicated that «تركوا» must be taken as being on the verge, not for what the author of al-Mughnī mentioned, but so that خافوا may properly occur as the apodosis, because fear is absent after death, so no fear can arise after leaving. If you say: what is the meaning of «لو تركوا» and its apodosis occurring as the ṣila of الذين? I say: its meaning is: let those fear whose description and state is that, if they were on the verge of leaving behind them offspring — and that is when death is upon them — they would fear for them being lost after them, because of the departure of their guardian and provider.

dervis-irab:10-10.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوالَ الْيَتامى ظُلْماً): resumptive speech introduced to forbid the wronging of orphans by guardians and executors. إن and its noun; the clause يأكلون is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; أموال اليتامى is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ظلما is a ḥāl (circumstantial) to be interpreted [as a derived form], i.e. being wrongdoers. You may parse it as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), the conditions for the accusative being fulfilled. You may also parse it as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) explaining the kind of eating, i.e. an eating of wrongdoing. (إِنَّما يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ ناراً وَسَيَصْلَوْنَ سَعِيراً): إنما is the restraining [ما] and the restrained [إن], with no governing effect; يأكلون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the واو is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the first إن; في بطونهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يأكلون, or to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of «نارا» and was then put first; نارا is a mafʿūl bihi; سيصلون is conjoined to يأكلون; سعيرا is a mafʿūl bihi.

* Rhetoric:
This verse contains a beautiful embodiment that appears in two of the devices of bayān:
1- Prolixity (ishāb) in their saying «في بطونهم»: He mentioned the bellies, because eating settles only in them, embodying the hideousness of the crime committed by eating the orphan's wealth. Like it is «قد بدت البغضاء من أفواههم», i.e. they mouthed it and said it with full mouths.
2- Majāz mursal (metonymic trope) in the eating of fire, the relation being causality: fire is not eaten; rather what is eaten is what causes it and leads to it, which is the orphan's wealth.
3- «يأكلون» came in the imperfect without the sīn of the future, and سيصلون with the sīn, because since the word «نارا» was unrestricted, it was restricted in His words «سعيرا», as that is the blazing embers.
4- Taʿrīḍ (allusion): by mentioning the bellies He alluded to their baseness and the lowliness of their state, which is the contemptibility of their souls [Translator's note: the source reads «وهو أن أنفسهم», evidently for «هوان أنفسهم»], and the Arabs held that to be blameworthy. Do you not see how al-Ḥuṭayʾa contented himself in his satire with this much, hinting at it, in his saying:
دع المكارم لا ترحل لبغيتها ... واقعد فإنك أنت الطاعم الكاسي
(Leave noble deeds — do not set out in quest of them; sit, for you are the one who is fed and clothed.)
i.e. the one fed and the one clothed.
[Translator's note: the source announces two devices but lists four.]

dervis-irab:92-92.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الدية): it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun); then it was applied to the wealth taken for killing (blood-money). One says: wadā, yadī, diyatan, like washā, yashī, shiyatan and washyan; the fāʾ (first radical) of the word was dropped.

* I'rab:
(وَما كانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ أَنْ يَقْتُلَ مُؤْمِناً إِلَّا خَطَأً) A resumptive statement brought to establish the rulings on killing. The wāw is resumptive; (ما) is negating, and here it has the sense of a prohibition entailing unlawfulness. (كان) is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; (لمؤمن) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of (كان); (أن يقتل مؤمنا) is an interpreted maṣdar, the postponed noun of (كان). (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). As for (خطأ), it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) interpreted as a derived word, i.e.:
"erring"; or accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e.: except by error; or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) by way of description, i.e.: an erroneous killing; or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). Al-Zamakhsharī put this last before the other views, saying: «If you ask: by what is خطأ accusative? I say: by its being an object of purpose (mafʿūl lahu), i.e.: it is not proper for him to kill him for any reason whatsoever except for error alone.»
In my view the views are equal; further discussion of it will come in the section of Benefits. (وَمَنْ قَتَلَ مُؤْمِناً خَطَأً فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ) The wāw is resumptive; (من) is a conditional jussive noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (قتل) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis); (مؤمنا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the i'rab of (خطأ) has already been discussed. (فتحرير): the fāʾ connects the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis), and (تحرير) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e.: "then upon him is the freeing of a slave" — and this is better and more fitting than making it the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e.: "then what is obligatory is the freeing of a slave". (مؤمنة) is an adjective of (رقبة). The nominal clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من». (وَدِيَةٌ مُسَلَّمَةٌ إِلى أَهْلِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَصَّدَّقُوا) The wāw is a conjunction, and (دية) is conjoined to (تحرير رقبة); (مسلمة) is an adjective, and (إلى أهله) is attached to (مسلّمة). (إلا أن يصدقوا) is an exception from the most general of states or the most general of times, i.e.: except in the state of giving charity — so it is a ḥāl — or "when they give in charity", so it is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (مسلمة). An expanded treatment of this will come in the section of Benefits. It has also been said that it is a disjoined exception (mustathnā munqaṭiʿ). (فَإِنْ كانَ مِنْ قَوْمٍ عَدُوٍّ لَكُمْ) The fāʾ is resumptive and (إن) is a conditional jussive particle; (كان) is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis, and the noun of (كان) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa"; (من قوم) is attached to an omitted khabar of (كان); (عدو) is an adjective of (قوم), and (لكم) is attached to an omitted adjective of (عدو). (وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ) The wāw is circumstantial; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (مؤمن) a khabar, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. (تحرير) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e.: "then upon him is the freeing of a slave"; its i'rab has already been given. (وَإِنْ كانَ مِنْ قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِيثاقٌ) The wāw is a conjunction and (إن) conditional; (كان) and its latent noun; (من قوم) is its khabar; (بينكم) is an adverb attached to an omitted fronted khabar, (بينهم) is conjoined to (بينكم), and (ميثاق) is a postponed mubtadaʾ. (فَدِيَةٌ مُسَلَّمَةٌ إِلى أَهْلِهِ) The fāʾ is connective; (دية) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e.: "then upon him is blood-money", and the reverse is also permissible, as already stated. (مسلمة) is an adjective, and (إلى أهله) is attached to (مسلمة). (وَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ) is conjoined to what precedes. (فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتابِعَيْنِ) The fāʾ is resumptive; (من) is a conditional jussive noun, a mubtadaʾ; (لم يجد) is in the position of the jussive as the protasis; the fāʾ connects the apodosis; (صيام) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, or the reverse; the clause (فصيام) is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; (شهرين) is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct) and (متتابعين) an adjective; and the protasis with its apodosis is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «من». (تَوْبَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً) (توبة) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e.: He legislated that for you as a mercy from Him and a means of repentance. It may also be accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e.: He turned to you in repentance (tāba ʿalaykum tawbatan). (من الله) is an adjective. The wāw is resumptive; (كان) and its noun, and (عليما حكيما) are its two khabars.

* Benefits:
1- On (خطأ):
I said in the I'rab that it is permissible to parse (خطأ) as a disjoined exception (mustathnā munqaṭiʿ) [Translator's note: the I'rab section above does not in fact list this option for خطأ; it mentions the disjoined exception only for «إلا أن يصدقوا»], because it is not of [the genus of] the first, and error does not fall under legal obligation (taklīf).
The meaning is: but if he kills by error, then its ruling is such-and-such. It is a fine parsing. Abū al-Baqāʾ and Abū Ḥayyān inclined to this parsing, and it is also what Sībawayh, al-Zajjāj and al-Ṭabarī chose. It belongs to the disjoined exception, which must be in the accusative, and which the people of Arabic call munqaṭiʿ. From it is the saying of Jarīr:
من البيض لم تظعن بعيدا ولم تطأ ... على الأرض إلا ريط برد مرحّل
(One of the fair women, who has not journeyed far, and has not trodden upon the ground except [upon] the hem of an embroidered cloak.)
He means: she has not trodden upon the ground except that she treads on the train of the cloak — and the train of the cloak is not part of the ground.

2- On «إلا أن يصدقوا»:
I said in the I'rab that it is permissible to make «أن يصدقوا» excepted from the most general of times, so that it is an adverb (ẓarf). Abū Ḥayyān considered this interpretation far-fetched, saying: «As for making an and what follows it an adverb, that is not permissible. The grammarians stated this explicitly and forbade saying «أجيئك أن يصيح الديك» (I will come to you that the cock crows) meaning the time of the cock's crowing. As for forming from it a maṣdar that would be in the place of a ḥāl, they likewise stated explicitly that it is not permissible. Sībawayh said, regarding the Arabs' saying «أنت الرجل أن تنازل وتخاصم» (you are the man to fight and dispute), in the sense of "you are the man for fighting and disputing", that the accusative is as an object of purpose (mafʿūl min ajlihi), because the future cannot be a ḥāl. So according to what we have established, its being a disjoined exception is the correct view.»

dervis-irab:93-93.t:
* I'rab:
(وَمَنْ يَقْتُلْ مُؤْمِناً مُتَعَمِّداً فَجَزاؤُهُ جَهَنَّمُ خالِداً فِيها) The wāw is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, brought to threaten the killer and to declare him criminal. (من) is a conditional jussive noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يقتل) is the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis); (مؤمنا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and (متعمدا) a ḥāl (circumstantial). (فجزاؤه): the fāʾ connects the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis); (جزاؤه) is a mubtadaʾ and (جهنم) its khabar (predicate), or the reverse; the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من». (خالدا) is a ḥāl, and (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خالدا». (وَغَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَلَعَنَهُ) The wāw conjoins to something implied (muqaddar) that is indispensable for the speech to cohere, and this implied element is indicated by the conditional sentence, i.e.: Allah has ruled that his recompense is that, and He is angry with him. (وَأَعَدَّ لَهُ عَذاباً عَظِيماً) is likewise conjoined.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse is the device of murāʿāt al-naẓīr (observing the congruent), which has been discussed before: it is that the speaker brings what suits the content. This verse is replete with words denoting anger, threat, menace, thunder and lightning, to indicate that the crime of killing is among the greatest of crimes and the most extreme in evil, because of the destruction of the edifice of society that results from it. How beautiful is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ in this regard: «This human being is the building of Allah; accursed is he who destroys His building.»

dervis-irab:94-94.t:
* Vocabulary:
(السَّلامَ), and al-salam with fatḥa on the sīn and the lām: greeting and surrender. It has been read with both.
(ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ): you travelled in it for trade or a military expedition.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا) Its i'rab has already been given. (إِذا ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَتَبَيَّنُوا) A resumptive statement brought to warn against rushing into killing. (إذا) is an adverb of future time (ẓarf) containing the meaning of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis; the clause (ضربتم) is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); (في سبيل الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ضربتم). The fāʾ connects the apodosis of (إذا); (تبينوا) is an imperative verb and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (وَلا تَقُولُوا لِمَنْ أَلْقى إِلَيْكُمُ السَّلامَ: لَسْتَ مُؤْمِناً) The wāw is a conjunction and (لا) is prohibitive; (تقولوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا), and the wāw is the fāʿil; (لمن) is attached to (تقولوا); the clause (ألقى إليكم السلام) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (إليكم) is attached to (ألقى), and (السلام) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «لست مؤمنا» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying), and (مؤمنا) is the khabar (predicate) of (لست). (تَبْتَغُونَ عَرَضَ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا) The clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of (تقولوا), i.e.: do not say that statement seeking booty and transient goods. (فَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ مَغانِمُ كَثِيرَةٌ) The fāʾ gives the reason (taʿlīliyya) for the prohibition, and the clause has no grammatical position; (عند الله) is an adverb attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (مغانم) is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) and (كثيرة) an adjective. (كَذلِكَ كُنْتُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَمَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ) The clause is resumptive, brought to liken their present state to the state they had been in. (كذلك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar of (كنتم); or the nominal kāf alone is the fronted khabar of (كنتم) and (ذلك) is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct). (من) is a preposition, and (قبل) is an adverb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning, attached to an omitted ḥāl. (فمنّ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and the clause (منّ الله) is conjoined to (كنتم); (عليكم) is attached to «منّ». (فَتَبَيَّنُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيراً) The grammarians in general made it a conjunction joining to the first (تبينوا), the command to ascertain being repeated for emphasis. In my view the fāʾ is al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), and there is no emphasis there, because the first command is specific to those whom you kill, while the second command is general, as though it establishes a comprehensive ruling, i.e.: if you know this and grasp its consequences, then ascertain.
(إن الله): (إن) and its noun; the clause of (كان) and what follows it is its khabar, and the clause is for giving the reason. (خبيرا) is the khabar of (كان); the clause (تعملون) has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of (ما); and (بما) is attached to «خبيرا».

dervis-irab:11-11.t:
* I'rab:
(يُوصِيكُمُ اللَّهُ فِي أَوْلادِكُمْ): resumptive speech introduced to begin detailing the rulings of inheritance given in summary in His words: «للرجال نصيب». يوصيكم is an imperfect verb; the كاف is its fronted object and الله its postponed fāʿil (agent); في أولادكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يوصيكم. (لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ): a resumptive clause introduced to explain the injunction. للذكر is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); مثل is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted, postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "a share like". So the clause is as if explaining the first, and it is in the position of accusative as the speech quoted by يوصيكم, because it has the sense of saying. The male is preferred with this advantage because he is the one responsible for providing, and because the female will turn, by virtue of the task entrusted to her, to managing the affairs of the house and caring for and raising the children; so that required making his share of the inheritance ample. (فَإِنْ كُنَّ نِساءً فَوْقَ اثْنَتَيْنِ فَلَهُنَّ ثُلُثا ما تَرَكَ): the فاء is of ramification (tafrīʿiyya), and the clause after it has no grammatical position because it is like a resumptive and causal clause; إن is conditional; كنّ is a defective past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the nūn is its noun and نساء its khabar; فوق is an adverb of place attached to an omitted adjective of نساء, i.e. exceeding two; it may also be a second khabar of كان. فلهن: the فاء links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); لهن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; ثلثا is the postponed mubtadaʾ, the sign of its nominative being the alif because it is dual; ما is a relative noun in the position of genitive by annexation; the clause ترك is the ṣila (relative clause); the clause فلهن ثلثا is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. (وَإِنْ كانَتْ واحِدَةً فَلَهَا النِّصْفُ): the واو is conjunctive; إن is conditional; كانت is a defective past verb, the تاء being the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine, and it is in the position of jussive as the protasis; its noun is latent (mustatir), the implied form being هي, i.e. the [female] child; واحدة is the khabar of كانت; the فاء links the apodosis; لها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; النصف is the postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. (وَلِأَبَوَيْهِ لِكُلِّ واحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا السُّدُسُ مِمَّا تَرَكَ إِنْ كانَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ): the واو is conjunctive, joining [this] to what preceded to begin the inheritance of ascendants. لأبويه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; لكل واحد is a preposition and its genitive noun; the apparent sense of the speech suggests that they are a badal (substitute) with repetition of the preposition, and this is what most parsers stated, al-Zamakhsharī at their head. He supported this substitution by saying: «Had it been said "ولأبويه السدس", the apparent sense would be that they share in it; and had it been said "ولأبويه السدسان", it would suggest dividing the two sixths between them equally or otherwise. If you say: why was it not said "ولكل واحد من أبويه السدس"? And what benefit is there in mentioning the two parents first and then substituting for them? I say: because in substitution and detailing after summarising there is emphasis and strengthening, like what you see in combining the thing explained with the explanation.» This is what al-Zamakhsharī said, and all the parsers and exegetes have transmitted it word for word; but there is a criticism of this i'rab, which you will see in the section of Benefits. منهما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of واحد; السدس is the postponed mubtadaʾ; مما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause ترك is the ṣila; إن is conditional; كان له ولد: كان with its fronted khabar and postponed noun; the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then to each one [is the sixth]"; and the conditional clause is resumptive. (فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ وَلَدٌ وَوَرِثَهُ أَبَواهُ): the فاء is resumptive; إن is conditional; لم is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; يكن is a defective imperfect verb, jussive; له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; ولد is its postponed noun; ورثه is conjoined to لم يكن; the هاء is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and أبواه the fāʿil. (فَلِأُمِّهِ الثُّلُثُ): the فاء links the apodosis; لأمه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; الثلث is the postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. (فَإِنْ كانَ لَهُ إِخْوَةٌ فَلِأُمِّهِ السُّدُسُ): conjoined to what preceded. (مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصِي بِها أَوْ دَيْنٍ): the words of the parsers and exegetes have been confused about what this preposition and its genitive noun attach to. Al-Zamakhsharī attached them to the preceding division of inheritances, not to what immediately follows them alone; al-Zamakhsharī means to say that they are attached to His words «يوصيكم الله» and what comes after it. In this attachment there is noticeable confusion, and therefore Abū Ḥayyān turned from it to attaching them to an omitted verb, i.e. they are entitled to that after a bequest. In this there is an impotent laxity and an evasion of attachment, which we wish to avoid in the Noble Qur'an. Abū al-Baqāʾ attached them to an omitted ḥāl from السدس, its implied form being "being due after a bequest", and this is more confused than the first two. So it is better to attach them — as I see it — to an omitted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. the division of these shares is after a bequest. The clause يوصي — with the active and the passive, and it has been read in both — is an adjective of وصية; أو is a conjunction for permitting both things; دين is conjoined to وصية. (آباؤُكُمْ وَأَبْناؤُكُمْ لا تَدْرُونَ أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ لَكُمْ نَفْعاً): the clause is parenthetical between His words «من بعد وصية» and His words «فريضة من الله». آباؤكم is a mubtadaʾ and أبناؤكم is conjoined to «آباؤكم»; the clause لا تدرون is the khabar; أيهم: an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and أقرب its khabar; the clause is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of تدرون because [the verb] has been suspended (ʿulliqa) by the interrogative; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أقرب; نفعا is a tamyīz (specification). أيّ may also be parsed — as Sībawayh says — as a relative, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, being the object of تدرون, with أقرب the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "they are nearer"; as for the second object of تدرون, it is omitted. Both aspects are acceptable and admissible. (فَرِيضَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً): فريضة is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb understood from the preceding clause, from the injunction; thus they parsed it. Against this is that فريضة is not a maṣdar but a فعيلة in the sense of مفعولة; so it is better to make it an emphatic ḥāl. من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of فريضة; إن and its noun; the clause كان عليما حكيما is its khabar; the clause of إن and what falls within its scope is causal, with no grammatical position.

* Benefits:
We said that all the parsers have joined in parsing «لكل واحد» as a badal with repetition of the preposition. Against this i'rab there is an objection that must be taken into account: on this supposition it would be a substitution of a thing for the [same] thing (badal al-shayʾ min al-shayʾ), the two being like one entity, and the original form of the speech would be: "and the sixth is for his two parents, for each one of them." The requirement of limiting oneself to the substituted-for [noun] is that the two share in the sixth, as He said: «فإن كن نساء فوق اثنتين فلهن ثلثا ما ترك», which required their sharing in it. But the badal — if the first were supposed to be disregarded — would require each of them to have the sixth individually, without sharing. This contradicts the nature of this kind of badal, because in this kind it is necessary that what the substituted-for and the substitute convey be one; its only benefit is emphasis by the combination of the two nouns, nothing else, with no additional meaning. So when the difference between them is established, the substitution mentioned becomes impossible. Nor may it properly be a badal of division (badal al-taqsīm) either on this i'rab, otherwise an additional meaning in the badal would be entailed [Translator's note: the source has «يدل التقسيم», evidently for «بدل التقسيم»]. So the right course then is to supply an omitted mubtadaʾ, as though it were said: "and for his two parents is a third"; then, having mentioned their share in summary, He detailed it with His words: "and for each one of them the sixth". The omission of the mubtadaʾ is permissible because the detailing necessarily indicates it, since each of them being entitled to a sixth entails both together being entitled to a third; and Allah knows best. Nor, on this view, is it sound to make it a badal of division. Do you not see that if you said: "The house, all of it, is for three: for Zayd, for ʿUmar and for Khālid", this would be a sound badal and division, because if you deleted the substituted-for and said: "The house is for Zayd, for ʿUmar and for Khālid", without adding anything in the badal, it would be sound. But if you said: "The house is for three: Zayd has a third of it, ʿAmr has a third of it and Khālid has a third of it", it would not be sound as a badal of division, because if you deleted the substituted-for the speech would become: "The house: Zayd has a third of it, ʿUmar has a third of it and Khālid has a third of it", and this is resumptive speech, because you have added to it the meaning of distinguishing what belongs to each one of them, which the substituted-for does not give; and in the badal of a thing for the [same] thing there is no room for additional meaning.
For this reason it was necessary to parse لكل واحد as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, as though it were said: "and for his two parents is a third", i.e. for each of them the sixth. This is a point of great subtlety.

dervis-irab:95-96.t:
* Vocabulary:
(غير أولي الضرر): i.e. those with disabilities, such as blindness, lameness, chronic illness and the like.

* I'rab:
(لا يَسْتَوِي الْقاعِدُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) A resumptive statement brought to explain the disparity of the ranks of the believers according to the disparity among them in jihād. (لا) is negating, and (يستوي) is an imperfect verb in the nominative, the ḍamma being implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ; (القاعدون) is its fāʿil (agent); (من المؤمنين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from «القاعدون» and from the pronoun concealed in it. (غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ وَالْمُجاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِأَمْوالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ) (غير) is a badal (substitute) from «القاعدون». We have not made it an adjective, because «غير» does not become definite through annexation, owing to its being steeped in indefiniteness, and it is not permissible for the adjective and the thing described to differ [in definiteness]. Al-Zamakhsharī paid no heed to what is established in grammar and made it an adjective. It may also be accusative as an exception, but the first is preferable, as is established in the books of grammar, because the speech is negated; and it has been read so [in the accusative].
It may also be genitive as an adjective of (المؤمنين); al-Aʿmash also read it in the genitive. A discussion of it will come in the section of Benefits. (أولي الضرر) is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct), genitive, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural. (المجاهدون) is conjoined to «القاعدون»; (في سبيل الله) is attached to «المجاهدون», and (بأموالهم) is also attached to it; (أنفسهم) is conjoined to «بأموالهم». (فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ الْمُجاهِدِينَ بِأَمْوالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ عَلَى الْقاعِدِينَ دَرَجَةً) The clause is explicative (mufassira), having no grammatical position, explaining the non-equality between the two groups. (فضل الله) is a verb and its fāʿil; (المجاهدين) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative by the yāʾ; the clause (فضل الله المجاهدين) explains the non-equality between the two groups. (بأموالهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «المجاهدين», and (أنفسهم) is conjoined to (أموالهم); (على القاعدين) is attached to (فضل). (درجة) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is the instrument of preference and of raising in rank, so it is like your saying: "I struck him a whip" (ḍarabtuhu sawṭan). Some parsed it as an adverb (ẓarf), and that is not far-fetched.
Others parsed it as a ḥāl, and it then requires an implied muḍāf, i.e.:
"possessors of a degree". Some said it is a tamyīz (specification), and there is no harm in this view.
What we have chosen is the most preferable. (وَكُلًّا وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْحُسْنى) The wāw is parenthetical; (كلّا) is a fronted mafʿūl bihi of «وعد», (الله) is the fāʿil, and (الحسنى) is the second mafʿūl bihi; the clause has no grammatical position because it is parenthetical. (وَفَضَّلَ اللَّهُ الْمُجاهِدِينَ عَلَى الْقاعِدِينَ أَجْراً عَظِيماً) The wāw is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes. (أجرا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq because it is synonymous with (فضل), or because it is its instrument, along the lines of
"a degree" and "a whip"; further discussion of it will come in the section of Benefits. (عظيما) is an adjective.
(دَرَجاتٍ مِنْهُ وَمَغْفِرَةً وَرَحْمَةً) (درجات) is a badal from «أجرا»; (منه) is attached to an omitted adjective of (درجات); (مغفرة) and (رحمة) are conjoined to (درجات). Al-Zamakhsharī put them in the accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq with their verb implied, in the sense: "and He forgave them and had mercy on them with forgiveness and mercy" — and perhaps this is better, for the sake of observing congruity. (وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً) The wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; (كان) and its noun, and (غفورا رحيما) are its two khabars (predicates); the clause is resumptive or circumstantial.

* Benefits:
What Ibn Yaʿīsh says:
Ibn Yaʿīsh said, when discussing «غير أولي الضرر»: «It has been read in the nominative, the genitive and the accusative. The nominative is as an adjective of «القاعدون»; its nominative cannot be as a badal in exception, because the implied form would then become: "None are equal except those with disability", and the meaning is not that; the meaning is only: the healthy who sit back and those who strive are not equal. The genitive is as an adjective of (المؤمنين), and the meaning is:
the healthy who sit back among the believers and those who strive are not equal — and the meaning in both is one. The accusative is as an exception.»

The grammarians between the badal and adjective analyses of (غير):
The grammarians have weighed [lit. wavered between] the badal and the adjective analyses of «غير». Whoever argued for the badal said: making «غير» an adjective requires interpretation, because «غير» does not become definite through annexation, and it is not permissible for the adjective and the thing described to differ in definiteness and indefiniteness; its interpretation is either that «القاعدون», since they are not specific individuals but the genus is meant by them, resemble the indefinite and so are described by it as the indefinite is described; or that «غير» may become definite when it occurs between two opposites. Whoever argued for the adjective said: its nominative cannot be as a badal in exception, because the implied form would then become: "the healthy who sit back and those who strive are not equal" — as Ibn Yaʿīsh said [Translator's note: so in the source; in the Ibn Yaʿīsh quotation above, the implied form that rules out the badal is "none are equal except those with disability", while "the healthy who sit back and those who strive are not equal" is given as the intended meaning]. This is one of their subtleties that indicate brilliance and keenness of mind, so reflect, and may Allah guide you.

Al-Zamakhsharī's view on the i'rab of (أجرا):
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Why are درجة, أجرا and درجات accusative? I say: His word «درجة» is accusative because it occupies the position of the single instance (al-marra) of preferring, as though it were said: He preferred them with one preference; its parallel is your saying: "he struck him a whip", in the sense: he struck him one blow.
As for أجرا, it is accusative by (فضل) because it has the sense of "He rewarded them with a reward"; and درجات and رحمة are a badal from أجرا. It is also permissible for «درجات» to be accusative in the way «درجة» is, as you say:
"he struck him whips", in the sense of blows — as though it were said: and He preferred him with preferences. And «أجرا عظيما» is accusative as a ḥāl from the indefinite noun «درجات», placed before it. And «مغفرة ورحمة» are accusative with their verb implied, in the sense: and He forgave them and had mercy on them with forgiveness and mercy.»

dervis-irab:97-99.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ ظالِمِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ) A resumptive statement establishing the state of a group who embraced Islam but did not emigrate, and were killed on the day of Badr along with the disbelievers — although emigration (al-hijra) was a pillar or a condition in Islam; then it was abrogated after the Conquest [of Mecca]. (إن) and its noun; the clause (توفاهم الملائكة) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The origin of (توفاهم) is (تتوفاهم); one of the two tāʾs was dropped according to the established rule. Ibn Jarīr and others allowed it to be a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, and that is not far-fetched. (الملائكة) is the fāʿil (agent) and (ظالمي أنفسهم) a ḥāl (circumstantial). As for the khabar (predicate) of (إن), it may be omitted, its implied form being: "Those whom the angels take [in death] perished"; or the khabar may be His saying: (قالوا فيم كنتم؟); or it may be:
(فأولئك مأواهم جهنم), the fāʾ entering the khabar redundantly (zāʾida) by likening the relative noun to a conditional noun. (قالُوا فِيمَ كُنْتُمْ؟) The pronoun in (قالوا) refers to the angels; the clause is either a khabar, as we stated before, or resumptive, explaining the omitted clause. (فيم):
(في) is a preposition, and the interrogative (ما) is in the position of the genitive by (في); its alif was dropped because the preposition entered upon it. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar of (كنتم), and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying). (قالُوا كُنَّا مُسْتَضْعَفِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ) The pronoun in (قالوا) refers to those whom the angels take; the clause of saying is resumptive, and the clause (كنا مستضعفين في الأرض) is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl; (مستضعفين) is the khabar of (كنا), and (في الأرض) is attached to (مستضعفين). (قالُوا: أَلَمْ تَكُنْ أَرْضُ اللَّهِ واسِعَةً فَتُهاجِرُوا فِيها) The pronoun in (قالوا) refers to the angels, and the clause is resumptive. The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī), for reproach; (لم) is a particle of negation, of conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning] and of the jussive; (تكن) is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by «لم»; (أرض الله) is the noun of (تكن) and (واسعة) its khabar; the clause is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl. The fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya); (تهاجروا) is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied (muḍmara) an after the fāʾ of causation, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (فيها) is attached to (تهاجروا). (فَأُولئِكَ مَأْواهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ) The fāʾ is connective because of the scent of condition in the relative noun; (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), (مأواهم) is a [second] mubtadaʾ, and (جهنم) is the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of the demonstrative. The clause (فأولئك) is either the khabar of «إن الذين», as we stated before, or resumptive.
(وَساءَتْ مَصِيراً) The wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; (ساءت) is a past verb of blame (dhamm); (مصيرا) is a tamyīz (specification), and the specifically blamed (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e.: Hell. (إِلَّا الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الرِّجالِ وَالنِّساءِ وَالْوِلْدانِ) (إلا) is a particle of exception, and (المستضعفين) are excepted from them because of their weakness and their inability to emigrate, so the exception is connected (muttaṣil). It has also been said:
the exception is disjoined (munqaṭiʿ), because those from whom the exception is made are either disbelievers or sinners by staying behind while being able to emigrate, so the oppressed weak are not included among them. (من الرجال) is attached to an omitted ḥāl, and (النساء) and (الولدان) are conjoined to (الرجال). (لا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ حِيلَةً وَلا يَهْتَدُونَ سَبِيلًا) The clause (لا يستطيعون) is an adjective of (المستضعفين). Describing a definite noun with a clause — which is indefinite — is permitted because the definite noun here does not refer to a specific thing in itself, along the lines of the poet's saying:
ولقد أمر على اللئيم يسبني ... فمضيت ثمّت قلت: لا يعنيني
(I pass by the base man who reviles me, and I go on, then say: "He does not mean me.")
(حيلة) is the object of (يستطيعون); the clause (ولا يهتدون) is conjoined to the clause (لا يستطيعون); (سبيلا) is the object of (يهتدون), or accusative by removal of the preposition — and perhaps that is more firmly grounded in eloquence — i.e.: to a way among the various ways. (فَأُولئِكَ عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَعْفُوَ عَنْهُمْ) The fāʾ is al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), because it occurs in the apodosis of an implied condition, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, i.e.: if you want to know their fate, then those... (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ; (عسى) is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb, one of the verbs of hope; (الله) is the noun of (عسى), and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is its khabar; the verbal clause is the khabar of the demonstrative. (وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَفُوًّا غَفُوراً) The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; (كان) and its noun, and (عفوا غفورا) are its two khabars.

dervis-irab:12-12.t:
* Vocabulary:
(كَلالَةً): maṣdar (verbal noun) of كلّ فلان, when he is neither a child nor a parent [of the deceased], i.e. he fell short (كلّ) of attaining the immediate kinship. Al-Ṭirimmāḥ said, describing the bull:
يهزّ سلاحا لم يرثه كلالة ... يشكّ به منها غموض المغابن
(He brandishes a weapon he did not inherit through distant kin, with which he pierces the hidden folds of their armpits.)
The scholars of jurisprudence and exegesis have spoken much about al-kalāla, and more will be said about this word in this sura.

* I'rab:
(وَلَكُمْ نِصْفُ ما تَرَكَ أَزْواجُكُمْ): the واو is a conjunction; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); نصف is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ما is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ترك is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; أزواجكم is the fāʿil (agent). (إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُنَّ وَلَدٌ): إن is conditional; لم is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; يكن is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and it is also the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); لهن is the fronted khabar of يكن and ولد its postponed noun; the conditional clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. (فَإِنْ كانَ لَهُنَّ وَلَدٌ): the فاء is conjunctive; إن is conditional; كان with its fronted khabar and postponed noun; the clause is conjoined. (فَلَكُمُ الرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكْنَ): the فاء is linking; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; الربع is the postponed mubtadaʾ; مما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause تركن is the ṣila; the clause joined with the فاء is the apodosis. (مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصِينَ بِها أَوْ دَيْنٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl; وصية is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause يوصين is a naʿt (adjective) of وصية; بها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يوصين; أو is a conjunction and دين is conjoined to وصية. (وَلَهُنَّ الرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكْتُمْ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَكُمْ وَلَدٌ فَإِنْ كانَ لَكُمْ وَلَدٌ فَلَهُنَّ الثُّمُنُ مِمَّا تَرَكْتُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ تُوصُونَ بِها أَوْ دَيْنٍ): the i'rab of all of this has been given before, so turn back to it. (وَإِنْ كانَ رَجُلٌ يُورَثُ كَلالَةً): the واو is conjunctive; إن is conditional; كان may be either defective (nāqiṣa) or complete (tāmma). If it is defective, رجل is its noun, the clause يورث, in the passive, is its khabar, and كلالة is a ḥāl. If it is complete, رجل is the fāʿil, the clause يورث is an adjective, and كلالة is a ḥāl. كلالة may also be parsed as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), its meaning then being kinship; or as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar if its meaning is inheritance, i.e. he is inherited from with an inheritance of kalāla. Some permitted it to be a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), but I do not find that acceptable. (أَوِ امْرَأَةٌ وَلَهُ أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌ): أو is a conjunction and امرأة is conjoined to رجل; وله: the واو is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; أخ is the postponed mubtadaʾ; أو is a conjunction and أخت is conjoined to أخ. (فَلِكُلِّ واحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا السُّدُسُ): the فاء is linking; لكل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; واحد is muḍāf ilayhi; منهما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of واحد; السدس is the postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause joined with the فاء is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. (فَإِنْ كانُوا أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذلِكَ فَهُمْ شُرَكاءُ فِي الثُّلُثِ): the فاء is resumptive; إن is conditional; كانوا is a defective past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis; the واو is the noun of كان and أكثر its khabar; من ذلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أكثر; the فاء is linking; هم is a mubtadaʾ and شركاء a khabar; في الثلث is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to شركاء. (مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصى بِها أَوْ دَيْنٍ): its i'rab has been given before, so renew your acquaintance with it. (غَيْرَ مُضَارٍّ وَصِيَّةً مِنَ اللَّهِ): غير مضار is a ḥāl from the pronoun of يوصى; وصية is an emphatic mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of يوصيكم; من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of وصية. (وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَلِيمٌ): the واو is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ, and عليم and حليم are its two khabars.

* Benefits:
1- A curious discussion:
Al-Shalawbīn said: it was related to me that a grammarian was asked about the i'rab of «كلالة» in the words of the Exalted: (وَإِنْ كانَ رَجُلٌ يُورَثُ كَلالَةً). He said: "Tell me: what is al-kalāla?" They told him: "The heirs when there is among them no father or higher, and no son or lower." He said: "Then it is a tamyīz (specification)." The explanation of his view is that the original form would be: «وإن كان رجل يرثه كلالة»; then the agent was omitted and the verb made passive, so the pronoun became nominative and latent; then كلالة was brought as a tamyīz.
Ibn Hishām's rejoinder:
Ibn Hishām replied to this grammarian, saying: «This grammarian was right in his question and wrong in his answer, for specifying by the agent after omitting it undoes the purpose for which it was omitted, and goes back on what the clause was built upon, namely folding away mention of the agent in it. For this reason there is nothing in their speech like: ضرب أخوك رجلا.» Ibn Hishām digressed, as is his habit, until he said: «The correct view in the verse is that «كلالة» is with an implied annexed noun, i.e. ذا كلالة (one of kalāla), and it is either a ḥāl from the pronoun of يورث — so «كان» is defective and يورث is the khabar, or complete and يورث is an adjective — or it is a khabar, and يورث is an adjective. Whoever explained «كلالة» as the deceased who left neither child nor parent, it is likewise a ḥāl or a khabar, but it does not need an implied omitted annexed noun. And whoever explained it as kinship, it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi.»
2- It is the custom of the Arabs, when they alternate between two nouns with أو, to refer the pronoun back to both of them together — you say: «من كان له أخ أو أخت فليصلهما» (whoever has a brother or a sister, let him keep ties with them both) — or to one of them, whichever you wish: you say «من كان له أخ أو أخت فليصله», and if you wish, «فليصلها».

dervis-irab:13-14.t:
* I'rab:
(تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ): resumptive speech introduced to explain that the preceding legislation is among the limits of Allah for His servants, so that they act by them and do not transgress them. تلك is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and حدود الله a khabar (predicate). (وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ يُدْخِلْهُ جَنَّاتٍ): the واو is resumptive; من is a jussivising conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ; يطع الله ورسوله is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); يدخله is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the هاء is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); جنات is accusative by removal of the preposition, or a second mafʿūl bihi by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa); the clause of the condition and the apodosis is in the position of nominative as the khabar.
(تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها): the clause تجري is a naʿt (adjective) of جنات; من تحتها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) تجري; الأنهار is the fāʿil (agent); خالدين is a ḥāl (circumstantial); فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خالدين. (وَذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ): the واو is circumstantial or resumptive; ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, الفوز a khabar and العظيم an adjective. (وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَيَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَهُ يُدْخِلْهُ ناراً خالِداً فِيها وَلَهُ عَذابٌ مُهِينٌ): its i'rab has been given before, so turn back to it.

* Rhetoric:
1- In this verse there is a strange device called «combining the differing and the agreeing» (jamʿ al-mukhtalifa wa-l-muʾtalifa). It is defined as the speaker intending to put on a par two persons praised, or two blamed, or two of whom one is praised and the other blamed, and then afterwards aiming to give one preference over the other in a way that does not detract from the other; so for the sake of that preference he brings meanings that differ from the meanings of equality. He put in the plural the pronoun of those abiding forever in the Garden, because everyone who enters the Garden abides in it forever, or because of the differing degrees of those abiding. As for the people of the Fire, among them are those who abide forever and those who do not, from the disobedient among the believers. So the plural was permissible there and was not permissible here [Translator's note: so in the source; the wording of «هناك» and «هنا» appears reversed relative to the reasoning given]. Because those abiding forever in the Fire are a single group, whereas those abiding forever in the Gardens are ranks according to the differences of their degrees. This is among the loftiest levels of bayān. Among its beautiful examples in poetry is the saying of al-Khansāʾ, when she wanted to put her brother Ṣakhr on a par in merit with her father while observing the right of the parent; she said:
جارى أباه فأقبلا وهما ... يتعاوران ملاة الحضر
وهما وقد برزا كأنهما ... صقرآن قد حطا على وكر
حتى إذا نزت القلوب وقد لزت هناك العذر بالعذر
وعلا هتاف الناس أيهما ... قال المجيب هناك: لا أدري
برقت صحيفة وجه والده ... ومضى على غلوائه يجري
أولى فأولى أن يساويه ... لولا جلال السنّ والكبر
(He raced his father, and the two came on, taking turns with the mantle of the race; the two, when they came out, were like two falcons alighting on a nest; until, when hearts leapt and cheek-straps were pressed against cheek-straps, and the people's shouting rose — "Which of them?" — the one answering there said: "I do not know"; the page of his father's face shone forth, and he went on running in his vigour; [the son] was very near to equalling him, were it not for the majesty of age and seniority.)
She put them on a par in boldness, plunging into the depths of war, speed in running and racing in the first line; الحضر, with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, is racing and running, and الملاة, with ḍamma on the mīm, is الريطة, which is any thin garment. Then in the second line she put them on a par by making them like two swift falcons. In the third line she wanted to describe the battle [Translator's note: so in the source; the line describes the race], and how some of the cheek-pieces (عذر) [of the horses] were pressed against others, which indicates equality in running. In the fourth line the people asked which of them was the father and which the son, because of how much they resembled each other. Then in the fifth line she ended by giving preference to the father through the shining of the page of his face, i.e. his face came out of the dust before the face of his competitor, by being ahead. In the sixth line she said that the son was able to equal the father were it not for the courtesy he kept, together with dutifulness to his father and knowledge of his right; so he held back his rein and lowered the wing of his merit, in order to prefer his father in merit over himself. Like it is [the verse] of Naṣr Allāh ibn Aḥmad al-Baṣrī, known as al-Khubzʾaruzzī, who was unlettered, baked rice-bread in Basra and recited love poetry. Of that is his saying:
رأيت الهلال ووجه الحبيب ... فكانا هلالين عند النظر
فلم أدر من حيرتي فيهما ... هلال السما من هلال البشر
ولولا التّورّد في الوجنتين ... وما لاح لي من خلال الشعر
لكنت أظن الهلال الحبيب ... وكنت أظن الحبيب القمر
(I saw the crescent and the face of the beloved, and they were two crescents to the sight; in my bewilderment over them I did not know the crescent of the sky from the crescent among mankind; were it not for the rosiness of the cheeks and what gleamed to me through the hair, I would have thought the crescent the beloved, and thought the beloved the moon.)
He first put them on a par, then turned back and preferred the beloved to the crescent.
2- Between the singular and the plural:
Abū al-Suʿūd al-ʿImādī, Mufti of Constantinople, leapt in his exegesis to the summit of acuity when he determined, by a happy inspiration, that the subtle point of the singular in His words «خالدا» is that it announces that entering the abode of punishment in a state of solitude is more severe in bringing on desolation, whereas the gatherings of the Garden are among close friends and loved ones, and gathering together is more conducive to dispelling desolation.

dervis-irab:15-16.t:
* I'rab:
(وَاللَّاتِي يَأْتِينَ الْفاحِشَةَ مِنْ نِسائِكُمْ): resumptive speech introduced to begin the rulings on the adulteress. The واو is resumptive; اللاتي is a relative noun; the clause يأتين الفاحشة is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; من نسائكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (فَاسْتَشْهِدُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ أَرْبَعَةً مِنْكُمْ): the فاء is linking, because of the flavour of condition in the relative noun; for that reason it is permissible for the command to be given as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) in His words استشهدوا. You may also make the khabar omitted, i.e. "in what is recited to you is the ruling on those who...". عليهن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to استشهدوا; أربعة is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective). (فَإِنْ شَهِدُوا فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ فِي الْبُيُوتِ): the فاء is resumptive; إن is conditional; شهدوا is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the فاء is linking; أمسكوهن is an imperative verb, the واو being the fāʿil (agent) and the هاء the mafʿūl bihi; في البيوت is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أمسكوهن; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (حَتَّى يَتَوَفَّاهُنَّ الْمَوْتُ أَوْ يَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ لَهُنَّ سَبِيلًا): حتى is a particle of limit and a preposition; يتوفاهن is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى; the هاء is a mafʿūl bihi and الموت the fāʿil; the implied أن and what falls within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of genitive by حتى, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to أمسكوهن; أو is a conjunction; يجعل is an imperfect verb conjoined to «يتوفاهن»; الله is the fāʿil; لهن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of «سبيلا» and was put first; سبيلا is a mafʿūl bihi. (وَالَّذانِ يَأْتِيانِها مِنْكُمْ فَآذُوهُما): the واو is a conjunction; اللذان is a mubtadaʾ, and by them He meant the adulterer and the adulteress; the clause يأتيانها is the ṣila, and the pronoun refers to الفاحشة; منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; the فاء is linking; آذوهما is an imperative verb, its agent and its direct object, and the clause is the khabar; its like has been given before. The meaning of الإيذاء (harming) is reviling, rebuking and beating. (فَإِنْ تابا وَأَصْلَحا فَأَعْرِضُوا عَنْهُما): فإن: the فاء is resumptive and إن conditional; تابا is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis; أصلحا is conjoined to «تابا»; the فاء is linking; the clause أعرضوا عنهما is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ تَوَّاباً رَحِيماً): إن and its noun; the clause of كان with its latent (mustatir) noun and its khabar is in the position of jussive as the apodosis [Translator's note: so in the source; it is evidently meant as the khabar of إن]; رحيما is the second khabar of كان.

dervis-irab:100-100.t:
* Vocabulary:
(المراغم), with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the dotted ghayn: a place to go, a stronghold, a place of movement; so it is a noun of place. It was used to convey that the emigrant rubs his people's noses in the dust, i.e. humiliates them. Al-raghm is humiliation and abasement; its origin is the nose sticking to al-raghām — with fatḥa on the rāʾ — which is dust. Raghima anfuhu raghman, of the pattern qatala:
a metonymy for humiliation, as though it stuck to the dust in abasement and humiliation. It becomes transitive with the alif, so one says: arghama Allāhu anfahu (may Allah rub his nose in the dust), and "I did it ʿalā raghmi anfihi" — with fatḥa or ḍamma on the rāʾ — i.e. I angered him; and "this is a targhīm for him", i.e. a humiliation. This is one of the idioms that run in their speech using the names of body parts without intending the parts themselves; rather, they assigned them to meanings other than the apparent ones, and the apparent sense of the names has no share in them by way of literal meaning. From this is their saying: "his speech is under my foot" and "his need is behind my back", meaning neglect and disregard. In al-Qāmūs: "al-raghm: aversion — and it is pronounced with any of the three vowels — like al-marghama; and raghimahu, like ʿalimahu and manaʿahu: he disliked it."

* I'rab:
(وَمَنْ يُهاجِرْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ يَجِدْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مُراغَماً كَثِيراً وَسَعَةً) A resumptive statement brought to explain the state of those who emigrate in the way of Allah. The wāw is resumptive; (من) is a conditional jussive noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يهاجر) is an imperfect verb, the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis); (في سبيل الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يهاجر); (يجد) is an imperfect verb, the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis); the protasis and its apodosis are in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «من». (مراغما) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), (كثيرا) an adjective, and (سعة) is conjoined to «مراغما». (وَمَنْ يَخْرُجْ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ مُهاجِراً إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ) The i'rab of its parallel has already been given; (مهاجرا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and (إلى الله ورسوله) is attached to «مهاجرا». (ثُمَّ يُدْرِكْهُ الْمَوْتُ فَقَدْ وَقَعَ أَجْرُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ) (ثم) is a conjunction, and (يدركه) is conjoined to (يخرج); the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi, and (الموت) is the fāʿil (agent) of (يدركه). (فقد): the fāʾ connects the apodosis, and (قد) is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); the clause (وقع أجره على الله) is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من»; (على الله) is attached to (وقع). (وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً) A resumptive clause; its i'rab has already been given.

dervis-irab:101-101.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُناحٌ) A resumptive statement brought to explain the rulings on shortening the prayer. The wāw is resumptive; (إذا) is an adverb of future time (ẓarf) containing the meaning of condition; the clause (ضربتم في الأرض) is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). The fāʾ connects the apodosis of (إذا); (ليس) is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; (عليكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of (ليس), and (جناح) is its postponed noun; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (أَنْ تَقْصُرُوا مِنَ الصَّلاةِ) The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e.: in shortening the prayer, and the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective of (جناح); (من الصلاة) is attached to (تقصروا). The discussion of shortening the prayer is treated at length in the books of jurisprudence. (إِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَنْ يَفْتِنَكُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) (إن) is conditional; (خفتم) is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and it is in the position of the jussive as the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis); (أن) and what falls within its scope form an interpreted maṣdar that is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (خفتم); (الذين كفروا) is the fāʿil, and the clause (كفروا) is a ṣila (relative clause). The conditional clause is resumptive, and the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: then there is no blame on you in shortening. (إِنَّ الْكافِرِينَ كانُوا لَكُمْ عَدُوًّا مُبِيناً) The clause gives the reason for the preceding permission to shorten. (إن) and its noun, and the clause (كانوا) is its khabar; the wāw is the noun of (كان); (لكم) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (عدوا) is the khabar of (كان), and (مبينا) an adjective.

dervis-irab:102-102.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا كُنْتَ فِيهِمْ فَأَقَمْتَ لَهُمُ الصَّلاةَ) The wāw is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, beginning the rulings on the prayer of fear (ṣalāt al-khawf). The address is to the Prophet ﷺ, and there is no proof in it for whoever held the view that the prayer of fear is not to be performed after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; rather, the address is comprehensive and covers every imam.
It is also permissible for the wāw to be a conjunction, so that the statement is joined to what precedes.
(إذا) is an adverb of future time (ẓarf) containing the meaning of condition; the clause (كنت) is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); the tāʾ is the noun of (كان), and (فيهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of (كنت). The pronoun refers to those travelling in the land or to those in fear; both are possible. The fāʾ is a conjunction; (أقمت) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (لهم) is attached to (أقمت); the clause is conjoined to the clause (كنت); and (الصلاة) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (فَلْتَقُمْ طائِفَةٌ مِنْهُمْ مَعَكَ) The fāʾ is connective; the lām is the lām of command; (تقم) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; (طائفة) is the fāʿil; (منهم) is attached to an omitted adjective; and (معك) is an adverb of place attached to (تقم). (وَلْيَأْخُذُوا أَسْلِحَتَهُمْ):
(وليأخذوا) is conjoined to (فلتقم), and (أسلحتهم) is a mafʿūl bihi. (فَإِذا سَجَدُوا فَلْيَكُونُوا مِنْ وَرائِكُمْ) The i'rab of its parallel has already been given; (من ورائكم) is attached to an omitted khabar of (فليكونوا). (وَلْتَأْتِ طائِفَةٌ أُخْرى لَمْ يُصَلُّوا فَلْيُصَلُّوا مَعَكَ) Likewise conjoined; the clause «لم يصلوا» is a second adjective of (طائفة); (فليصلوا) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and (معك) is an adverb of place attached to (فليصلوا). (وَلْيَأْخُذُوا حِذْرَهُمْ وَأَسْلِحَتَهُمْ) Likewise conjoined. (وَدَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْ تَغْفُلُونَ عَنْ أَسْلِحَتِكُمْ وَأَمْتِعَتِكُمْ) The clause is resumptive, brought to stress extra caution, because the enemy supposes that the prayer is a likely occasion for laying down arms. (ود الذين) is a verb and its fāʿil; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (لو) is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), so it is a particle-relative (mawṣūl ḥarfī), and together with what follows it forms a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the accusative because it is the object of (تود) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb in the verse is ودّ]. The clause (تغفلون) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the particle-relative; (عن أسلحتكم) is attached to (تغفلون), and (أمتعتكم) is conjoined to (أسلحتكم). (فَيَمِيلُونَ عَلَيْكُمْ مَيْلَةً واحِدَةً) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and (يميلون) is conjoined to (تغفلون); (عليكم) is attached to (يميلون); (ميلة) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and (واحدة) an adjective. (وَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِنْ كانَ بِكُمْ أَذىً مِنْ مَطَرٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is the lā of generic negation and (جناح) its noun; (عليكم) is attached to an omitted khabar of «لا». (إن) is conditional; (كان) is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive as the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis); (بكم) is attached to the omitted fronted khabar of (كان), and (أذى) is its postponed noun; (من مطر) is attached to an omitted adjective of (أذى). The jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: then there is no blame on you. (أَوْ كُنْتُمْ مَرْضى أَنْ تَضَعُوا أَسْلِحَتَكُمْ) (أو) is a conjunction, and (كنتم) is conjoined to (كان بكم أذى); (مرضى) is the khabar of (كنتم). (أن تضعوا) is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e.: in that you lay down; the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (جناح) or to an omitted adjective of it; (أسلحتكم) is a mafʿūl bihi. (وَخُذُوا حِذْرَكُمْ) Likewise conjoined. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ أَعَدَّ لِلْكافِرِينَ عَذاباً مُهِيناً) (إن) and its noun; the clause (أعد للكافرين) is its khabar; (عذابا) is the object of (أعد), and (مهينا) an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
