(الواو) resumptive; (لولا) a non-jussive conditional particle — of non-occurrence because of occurrence (imtināʿ li-wujūd) — (فضل) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, and the khabar (predicate) is necessarily omitted, its implied form being "موجود" ("existing"); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (على) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (فضل); (الواو) conjunction; (رحمة) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to فضل, nominative like it, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لولا; (همت) a past verb ... and (التاء) for the feminine; (طائفة) fāʿil (agent), nominative; (من) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of طائفة; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (يضلّوا) an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb), the sign of the subjunctive being the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يضلوك) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, its implied form being بأن يضلّوك ... attached to (همت).
(الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) [Note: Or parenthetical, and the clause after it is parenthetical with no grammatical position.] , (ما) negative; (يضلّون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (إلا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (أنفس) mafʿūl bihi, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction — or resumptive — (ما يضرون) like ما يضلّون ...
and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (من) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (شيء) genitive in form, accusative in position, a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it is of the kind of a description of the maṣdar, i.e.: ما يضرونك ضررا ما ("they do not harm you with any harm"). (الواو) resumptive; (أنزل) a past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (عليك) like the first, attached to (أنزل); (الكتاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (الحكمة) maʿṭūf to الكتاب, accusative like it; (الواو) conjunction; (علّم) like أنزل, and the fāʿil is "huwa", and (الكاف) mafʿūl bihi; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as second mafʿūl bihi; (لم) a particle of negation, the jussive and inversion (of tense); (تكن) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), its noun a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت"; (تعلم) an imperfect verb, nominative, and its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنت"; (الواو) conjunction; (كان) an incomplete past verb; (فضل) the noun of كان, nominative; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (عليك) like the first, attached to (فضل); (عظيما) the khabar of كان, accusative.
The clause «لولا فضل الله ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «همّت طائفة» has no grammatical position, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition [Note: The apodosis may be implied, i.e. لأضلوك ("they would have led you astray"), and the clause همّت resumptive, i.e. لقد همّت ("indeed a party intended") (Ḥāshiyat al-Jamal ʿalā al-Jalālayn).] .
The clause «ما يضلّون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of يضلّوك.
The clause «ما يضرونك ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the ḥāl clause ... or it has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أنزل الله ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «علّمك ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أنزل الله.
The clause «تكن ...» has no grammatical position, ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «تعلم ...» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of تكن.
The clause «كان فضل الله ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أنزل الله.

safi-cedvel:137-137.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna; (آمنوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (ثم) a conjunction in the four places; (كفروا، آمنوا، كفروا، ازدادوا) like آمنوا; (كفرا) tamyīz (specification), accusative (manṣūb); (لم) a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; (يكن) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of يكن, nominative (marfūʿ); (اللام) the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd); (يغفر) an imperfect verb, subjunctive by أن obligatorily implied after the lām of denial, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يغفر).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يغفر) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of يكن.
(الواو) conjunctive; (لا) negating; (ليهدي) like ليغفر, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو", i.e. Allah.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يهديهم) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, maʿṭūf (conjoined) on the first interpreted maṣdar.
(سبيلا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «إنّ الذين آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause آمنوا.
The (second) clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause كفروا.
The (second) clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the (second) clause آمنوا.
The clause «ازدادوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the second clause كفروا.
The clause «لم يكن الله ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «يغفر لهم» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «يهديهم ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second particle relative (أن).

* Benefits:
- The lām of denial — His saying, the Exalted, ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾: in ليغفر the lām is the lām of denial, and يغفر is subjunctive by the أن implied after it. This lām is called the lām of denial, and the imperfect after it is made subjunctive by an implied أن, like the lām of cause; or rather, the lām of cause preceded by a negated form of kāna is called the lām of denial.

safi-cedvel:138-138.t:
* I'rab:
(بشّر) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت"; (المنافقين) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (الباء) a preposition; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of anna; (عذابا) the noun of anna, accusative; (أليما) naʿt (adjective), accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ لهم عذابا ...) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (بشّر).
The clause «بشّر ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
Sarcasm (tahakkum): in His saying, the Exalted, ﴿بَشِّرِ﴾, «بشّر» ("give glad tidings") is put in the place of "warn", in sarcasm towards them.

safi-cedvel:139-139.t:
* I'rab:
(الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of المنافقين in the previous verse «[Note: or it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هم" ... and the nominal clause has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
(2) Or [attached] to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of يتخذ, i.e. "they take the disbelievers as allies, passing over, in their taking, the taking of the believers" (al-Jumal).]» [Translator's note: the source has run footnote (2), which belongs to (من دون) below, into this footnote.]; (يتخذون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الكافرين) first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (أولياء) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and it is barred from nunation, its pattern أفعلاء; (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أولياء «2»; (المؤمنين) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (الهمزة) for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī); (يبتغون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (عند) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (يبتغون), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (العزّة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الفاء) causal, conveying the cause in place of the answer to the question «[Note: and the implied answer is ... "seeking honour with them is vain, for honour belongs to Allah".]»; (إن العزة لله) a particle resembling the verb, its accusative noun and its khabar; (جميعا) ḥāl, accusative, emphasizing the content of the clause.
The clause «يتخذون ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «يبتغون ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إنّ العزة لله ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive and causal.

safi-cedvel:140-140.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (قد) a particle of realization; (نزل) a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; (على) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نزّل); (في الكتاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نزّل); (أن) lightened from the heavy [أنّ], and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); (إذا) an adverb of future time, in the position of the accusative, attached to the content of the apodosis; (سمعتم) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and its fāʿil [Translator's note: the sentence breaks off thus in the source]; (آيات) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (يكفر) an imperfect verb, passive, nominative (marfūʿ); (بها) in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (الواو) conjunctive; (يستهزأ) like يكفر, and the nāʾib fāʿil is (بها); (الفاء) the connective of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (لا) prohibitive, making the verb jussive; (تقعدوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (مع) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (تقعدوا), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (حتى) a particle of limit and genitive; (يخوضوا) an imperfect verb, subjunctive by an implied أن after حتى, the sign of the subjunctive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يخوضوا) is in the position of the genitive by (حتى), attached to (تقعدوا).
(في حديث) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يخوضوا); (غير) a naʿt (adjective) of حديث, genitive like it, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن إذا سمعتم) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of (نزل).
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna; (إذا) a particle of answer with no governing effect; (مثل) the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إنّ) like the first; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative; (جامع) khabar, nominative; (المنافقين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (الواو) conjunctive; (الكافرين) maʿṭūf (conjoined) on المنافقين, genitive like it; (في جهنم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to جامع, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa because it is a diptote; (جميعا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from المنافقين and الكافرين, its governor being (جامع) «[Note: what permitted the ḥāl to come from the muḍāf ilayhi is that the muḍāf is the governor of the ḥāl.]».
The clause «قد نزّل عليكم» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «of the condition, its protasis and its apodosis» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of أن.
The clause «سمعتم ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يكفر بها» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from آيات الله.
The clause «يستهزأ بها» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined on the ḥāl clause.
The clause «لا تقعدوا» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يخوضوا» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «إنّكم ... مثلهم» has no grammatical position, causal and resumptive, affirming the content of the apodosis understood from the context of the speech by the use of (إذن), i.e. "you, if you sit with them, are like them".
The clause «إن الله جامع ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(جامع): an active participle from the triliteral جمع, its pattern فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
1- «وَقَدْ نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ» is an address to the hypocrites by way of iltifāt (shift of address), conveying the intensification of the rebuke that the enumeration of their crimes calls for.
2- Simile (tashbīh): in His saying «إِنَّكُمْ إِذاً مِثْلُهُمْ». The likeness between the disbelievers and the hypocrites appears in the verse between those sitting and those sat with; for those who side with the disbelievers, ally with them and stretch out hands of abasement and humiliation to them, while able to stand firm and defy, are like the disbelievers.

* Benefits:
1- His saying, the Exalted, ﴿إِنَّكُمْ إِذاً مِثْلُهُمْ﴾: إذن is a particle of answer and requital, and here it is inoperative, with no governing effect, because it falls between the noun of inna and its khabar. Discussion of it has preceded in detail in this same sūra, verse (53).
2- His saying, the Exalted, ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ جامِعُ الْمُنافِقِينَ وَالْكافِرِينَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ جَمِيعاً﴾: جميعا is a ḥāl, accusative. If it comes accusative and nunated, it is a ḥāl, as in جاء المدعوون جميعا ("the invited came all together").
But if it is attached to a pronoun referring to the noun before it, it is tawkīd (emphasis), as in: جاء المدعوون جميعهم ("the invited came, all of them").

safi-cedvel:141-141.t:
* I'rab:
(الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of المنافقين in the previous verse «[Note: or it is a badal (substitute) from it ... or a badal from the previous relative in His saying: الذين يتخذون الكافرين ..., because the address is with the believers.]»; (يتربصون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الباء) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يتربصون); (الفاء) resumptive; (إن) a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive; (كان) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (لكم) like بكم, attached to the fronted khabar (predicate) of kāna; (فتح) the delayed noun of kāna, nominative; (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt of فتح; (قالوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الهمزة) for interrogation; (لم) a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; (نكن) an incomplete imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "نحن"; (معكم) an adverb of place, accusative (manṣūb), attached to the khabar of نكن ... and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) conjunctive; (إن كان ... نستحوذ) like its counterpart above; (عليكم) like بكم, attached to (نستحوذ); (الواو) conjunctive; (نمنع) an imperfect verb, jussive, maʿṭūf (conjoined) on نستحوذ, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is "naḥnu"; (من المؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نمنعكم), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (الفاء) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (يحكم) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; (بين) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (يحكم), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يحكم); (القيامة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunctive; (لن) a particle of negation, subjunctive and the future; (يجعل) an imperfect verb, subjunctive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (للكافرين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يجعل), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (على المؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (سبيلا) «[Note: or attached to (يجعل).]», which is mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «يتربصون ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «كان لكم فتح» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «قالوا» has no grammatical position, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a jussive condition not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «لم نكن معكم» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «كان للكافرين نصيب» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause كان لكم فتح.
The (second) clause «قالوا» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a jussive condition not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «لم نستحوذ ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «نمنعكم» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined on the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «الله يحكم ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive «[Note: it is permissible for it to be conjoined on the previous resumptive clause.]».
The clause «يحكم بينكم» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «لن يجعل الله ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause الله يحكم.

* Morphology:
(فتح): an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb فتح يفتح, of the third bāb, its pattern فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- «الَّذِينَ يَتَرَبَّصُونَ بِكُمْ» is a variation of the address (talwīn al-khiṭāb) and its turning to the believers, enumerating some others of the crimes and vile deeds of the hypocrites.
2- If you say: why did He call the victory of the Muslims a "conquest" (فتح) and the victory of the disbelievers a "share" (نصيب)?
I say: to magnify the standing of the Muslims and to belittle the lot of the disbelievers, because the victory of the Muslims is a great matter for which the gates of heaven are opened so that it descends upon His friends; as for the victory of the disbelievers, it is nothing but a lowly lot and a morsel of this world that they obtain. And calling the victory the Muslims attained a "conquest" is of the type of majāz mursal (metonymic trope), in view of what the victory leads to.

safi-cedvel:142-142.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (المنافقين) the noun of inna, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (يخادعون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (الواو) circumstantial; (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (خادع) khabar (predicate), nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) conjunctive; (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second (قاموا); (قاموا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (إلى الصلاة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قاموا); (قاموا) like the first; (كسالى) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (يراءون) an imperfect verb like يخادعون; (الناس) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) conjunctive; (لا) negating; (يذكرون الله) like يخادعون الله; (إلا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (قليلا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), for it is its description «[Note: or a mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), accusative, standing in for the adverb, for it is its description, i.e. "except for a little time".]», accusative, i.e. "except a little remembrance".
The clause «إنّ المنافقين ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يخادعون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «هو خادعهم» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl «[Note: it is permissible for it to be conjoined on the khabar clause of inna, and permissible for it to be resumptive.]».
The clause «قاموا إلى الصلاة» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قاموا كسالى» has no grammatical position, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; and the condition, its protasis and apodosis are conjoined on the khabar of inna.
The clause «يراءون ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl «[Note: it is permissible for it to be resumptive, and so to have no grammatical position.]».
The clause «لا يذكرون ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined on the clause يراءون.

* Morphology:
(خادع): an active participle from the triliteral خدع, on the pattern فاعل, and it has been annexed to the object.
(كسالى): plural of كسل or كسلان, from كسل يكسل, of the bāb فرح; the pattern of كسل is فعل with fatḥa then kasra, the pattern of كسلان is فعلان with fatḥa on the fāʾ, and the pattern of كسالى is فعالى with ḍamma on the fāʾ; the fatḥa is also permissible in a different reading.
(يراءون): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is يرائيون; the vowel was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made quiescent — iʿlāl by making quiescent — and the hamza was given its vowel; two quiescent letters met, so the first was deleted to escape the meeting of two quiescents; its pattern is يفاعون.

* Rhetoric:
«وَهُوَ خادِعُهُمْ»
That is, He does with them what the one who prevails in deception does, in that He left them in this world with their blood and property protected, and prepared for them in the Hereafter the lowest depth of the Fire.
And His deception, Glorified and Exalted is He, is of the type of mushākala (verbal correspondence).

safi-cedvel:143-143.t:
* I'rab:
(مذبذبين) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb), from the fāʿil (agent) of يراءون, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (بين) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) مذبذبين; (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and (اللام) the lām of distance and (الكاف) for address; (لا) negating; (إلى) a preposition; (ها) a particle of alerting; (أولاء) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted ḥāl from the pronoun of مذبذبين, which is its governor, i.e. "not attributed to these ..."; (الواو) conjunctive; (لا إلى هؤلاء) like the first; (الواو) resumptive; (من) a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (يضلل) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ); (الفاء) the connective of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (لن) a particle of negation and subjunctive; (تجد) an imperfect verb, subjunctive, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت"; (اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a ḥāl from (سبيلا) «[Note: or attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi, if (تجد) is taken as transitive to two objects.]», which is mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «يضلل الله ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لن تجد ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of a jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(مذبذبين): plural of مذبذب, a passive participle from the quadriliteral ذبذب, its pattern مفعلل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the first lām.

* Rhetoric:
«مُذَبْذَبِينَ بَيْنَ ذلِكَ», i.e. wavering between the two, bewildered, Satan having made them waver. The origin of al-dhabdhaba is the sound of the movement of a hanging thing; then it was borrowed (istiʿāra) for every agitation and movement.

* Benefits:
His saying, the Exalted, about the hypocrites: ﴿مُذَبْذَبِينَ بَيْنَ ذلِكَ لا إِلى هؤُلاءِ وَلا إِلى هؤُلاءِ﴾ — this verse draws a wonderful artistic picture of the state of the hypocrites: they are forever swinging and shaking, never settling or holding firm in one state. The words of this verse and its meanings come to share in drawing this picture: the adjective (مذبذبين), by its sound and rhythm, depicts the trembling and constant shaking that never settles, and His saying, the Exalted, ﴿لا إِلى هؤُلاءِ وَلا إِلى هؤُلاءِ﴾ depicts the swinging and lack of steadiness. It is a picture that the imagination and the senses contemplate more wonderfully than what the eye sees and the artist's brush draws.

safi-cedvel:144-144.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab has passed «[Note: in verse (135) of this sūra.]»; (لا) prohibitive, making the verb jussive; (تتخذوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الكافرين) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (أولياء) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أولياء «[Note: or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun latent in أولياء, or from the fāʿil of (تتخذوا) ... and see verse (139) of this sūra.]»; (المؤمنين) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (الهمزة) for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī); (تريدون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (تجعلوا) an imperfect verb, subjunctive, the sign of the subjunctive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تجعلوا) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being تريدون.
(لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of the verb تجعلوا; (على) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted ḥāl from (سلطانا) «[Note: see the i'rab of verse (91) of this sūra.]» — a naʿt (adjective) that came before what it qualifies —; (سلطانا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (مبينا) naʿt, accusative.
The vocative clause «أيها الذين ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لا تتخذوا» has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
The clause «تريدون ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «تجعلوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).

safi-cedvel:147-147.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (يفعل) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative; (بعذاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يفعل), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إن) a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive; (شكرتم) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) ... and (تم) a pronoun, fāʿil; (الواو) conjunctive; (آمنتم) like شكرتم.
(الواو) resumptive; (كان) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of kāna, nominative; (شاكرا) the khabar (predicate) of kāna, accusative (manṣūb); (عليما) a second khabar, accusative.
The clause «يفعل الله» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «شكرتم» has no grammatical position, resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "if you are grateful, then what would Allah do with punishing you?".
The clause «آمنتم» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause شكرتم.
The clause «كان الله شاكرا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Benefits:
Interrogative ما: it is an indeclinable noun, and it falls in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) in the following cases:
1- When a noun follows it, as in: ما ليلة القدر؟ ("What is the Night of Decree?")
2- When an intransitive verb follows it, as in: ما يقوم مقامك؟ ("What takes your place?")
3- When a transitive verb follows it that has taken its full object, as in: ما حملك على ذلك؟ ("What led you to that?")
And it is parsed as a fronted mafʿūl bihi when a transitive verb follows it that has not taken its object, as in: ما تشاء مني؟ ("What do you want from me?"), ما قرأت؟ ("What did you read?").
And it is parsed as in the position of the accusative as the khabar of kāna or one of its sisters when an incomplete verb follows it, as in:
ما أصبح عملك؟ ("What has your work become?"), ما كان شأنك؟ ("What was your affair?").
Remark: sometimes ذا enters upon it, so that it becomes ماذا. Then either we parse the whole as a single compound in such-and-such a position according to what we have mentioned, or «ما» is parsed as an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and ذا as a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as khabar.

safi-cedvel:145-146.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ المنافقين) as the previous one «[Note: in verse (142) of this sūra.]»; (في الدرك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of inna; (الأسفل) a naʿt (adjective) of الدرك, genitive (majrūr) like it; (من النار) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الدرك; (الواو) conjunctive; (لن تجد لهم نصيرا) like لن تجد له سبيلا «[Note: in verse (143) of this sūra.]».
The clause «إنّ المنافقين ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لن تجد لهم ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined on the khabar of inna «[Note: it is permissible for it to be resumptive.
The yāʾ was dropped from the Quranic script for lightness, because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
(2, 3) Some permitted making it the khabar of the relative (الذين), taking it as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and taking the fāʾ as redundant (zāʾida).]» [Translator's note: the source has run footnotes 2 and 3, which belong to (يؤتي) and to the clause «أولئك مع المؤمنين» below, into this footnote.]
(إلا) a particle of exception; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as the excepted in a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); (تابوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الواو) conjunctive; (أصلحوا) like تابوا; (الواو) conjunctive; (اعتصموا) like تابوا; (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (اعتصموا); (الواو) conjunctive; (أخلصوا) like تابوا; (دين) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (لله) like بالله, attached to (أخلصوا); (الفاء) resumptive — or redundant, for linking, because of the sense of condition in the speech connected with الذين —; (أولئك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ ... and (الكاف) for address; (مع) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; (المؤمنين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (الواو) conjunctive; (سوف) a particle of the future; (يؤتي) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ «2»; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (المؤمنين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (أجرا) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (عظيما) naʿt, accusative.
The clause «تابوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «أصلحوا» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the ṣila clause.
The clause «اعتصموا» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the ṣila clause.
The clause «أخلصوا» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the ṣila clause.
The clause «أولئك مع المؤمنين» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) «3».
The clause «سوف يؤتي الله» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause أولئك مع ...

* Morphology:
(الدرك): a noun for the furthest bottom of Hell, its pattern فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(الأسفل): a derived adjective from سفل يسفل, of the bāb نصر, the bāb فرح and the bāb كرم, its pattern أفعل, and it carries the sense of preference (tafḍīl).

safi-cedvel:148-148.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) negating; (يحبّ) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); (الله) fāʿil (agent), nominative; (الجهر) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (بالسوء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) الجهر; (من القول) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from السوء; (إلّا) a particle of exception; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as the excepted in a continuous exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil) from the word الجهر بالسوء, and that is with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "except the public utterance of one who has been wronged" «[Note: or [excepted] from the implied thing excepted from, which is (من أحد); it is also permissible for it to be in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from the word excepted from ... and it is permissible for the exception to be discontinuous.]»; (ظلم) a past verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو", and it is the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid); (الواو) resumptive; (كان) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of kāna, nominative; (سميعا) the khabar (predicate) of kāna, accusative; (عليما) a second khabar, accusative.
The clause «لا يحبّ الله ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «ظلم ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «كان الله سميعا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(الجهر): an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb جهر يجهر, of the bāb فتح, its pattern فعل with fatḥa then sukūn; and there are other maṣdars, namely جهارا with kasra on the jīm, and جهرة with the addition of tāʾ marbūṭa «[Note: and see verse (55) of Sūrat al-Baqara.]».

* Rhetoric:
His not loving something, Glorified and Exalted is He, is a kināya (metonymy) for His anger.

safi-cedvel:149-149.t:
* I'rab:
(إن) a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive; (تبدوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is an attached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent); (خيرا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (أو) a conjunction; (تخفوا) like تبدوا and maʿṭūf (conjoined) on it, and (الهاء) an attached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (أو) a conjunction; (تعفوا) like تبدوا and conjoined on it; (عن سوء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تعفوا); (الفاء) the connective of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) — or causal —; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative; (كان) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; (عفوا) the khabar (predicate) of kāna, accusative; (قديرا) a second khabar, accusative.
The clause «إن تبدوا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تخفوه» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the resumptive clause.
The clause «تعفوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the resumptive clause.
The clause «إنّ الله كان ...» has no grammatical position, causal, giving the cause of the omitted apodosis, which is: "then pardon is better for you".
The clause «كان عفوا ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of inna.

* Morphology:
(تبدوا - تخفوا - تعفوا): they contain iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, in that the weak letter — the lām of the word — was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters «[Note: and see verse (33) of Sūrat al-Baqara.]».

safi-cedvel:152-152.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunctive; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (آمنوا بالله ورسله) like يكفرون بالله ورسله above «[Note: in verse (150) of this sūra.]», though the verb here is past; (الواو) conjunctive; (لم) a particle of negation and jussive; (يفرّقوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (بين) an adverb of place, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يفرّقوا); (أحد) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (من) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of أحد; (أولئك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ.. and (الكاف) a particle of address; (سوف) a particle of the future; (يؤتي) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو", and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (أجور) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) resumptive; (كان الله غفورا رحيما) like كان الله عفوّا قديرا «[Note: in verse (149) of this sūra.]».
The clause «الذين آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the resumptive clause «[Note: in verse (150) of this sūra.]».
The clause «آمنوا بالله ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative.
The clause «لم يفرّقوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the ṣila clause.
The clause «أولئك سوف يؤتيهم ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «سوف يؤتيهم ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
The clause «كان الله غفورا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

safi-cedvel:150-151.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna, the particle resembling the verb; (يكفرون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يكفرون); (الواو) conjunctive; (رسل) maʿṭūf (conjoined) on the Name of Majesty, genitive (majrūr) like it, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) conjunctive; (يريدون) like يكفرون; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (يفرّقوا) an imperfect verb, subjunctive, the sign of the subjunctive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يفرّقوا) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being يريدون.
(بين) an adverb of place, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (يفرّقوا); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi; (رسل) conjoined on the Name of Majesty by the wāw, genitive like it, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunctive; (يقولون) like يكفرون; (نؤمن) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "نحن"; (ببعض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نؤمن); (الواو) conjunctive; (نكفر ببعض) like نؤمن ببعض; (الواو) conjunctive; (يريدون أن يتّخذوا) like يريدون أن يفرّقوا; (بين) like the first, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi whose governor is يتّخذوا; (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address; (سبيلا) first mafʿūl bihi, accusative, i.e. "to take a middle position between faith and disbelief".
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يتّخذوا) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being the second يريدون.
The clause «إنّ الذين يكفرون ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يكفرون ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «يريدون ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the ṣila clause.
The clause «يفرّقوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «يقولون» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause يريدون.
The clause «نؤمن ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «نكفر ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined on the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The (second) clause «يريدون» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the (first) clause يريدون.
The clause «يتّخذوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
(151) (أولئك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).. and (الكاف) a particle of address; (هم) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) «[Note: or a nominative pronoun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar (predicate) is الكافرون, and the clause هم الكافرون is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.]»; (الكافرون) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (حقّا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and it emphasizes the content of the clause before it; (الواو) resumptive; (أعتدنا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn..
and (نا) an attached pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil; (للكافرين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أعتدنا); (عذابا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (مهينا) naʿt (adjective), accusative.
The clause «أولئك هم الكافرون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «أعتدنا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
Putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun: in His saying, the Exalted, ﴿وَأَعْتَدْنا لِلْكافِرِينَ﴾, where the overt noun was put in place of the pronoun, as a reminder of the hideous attribute of disbelief, which signals the cause.

* Benefits:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْكافِرُونَ حَقًّا﴾ — حقا has two parsings. The first: a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, its implied form being "that is truly true" (حقّ ذلك حقا). The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied sense being "those are the disbelievers without doubt". But the stronger is that it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, since it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and the maṣdar is non-derived (jāmid), whereas the ḥāl comes derived ... unless it can be interpreted by a derived word, as in: كرّ عليّ أسدا ("he charged at me [like] a lion"), which you interpret as كرّ عليّ شجاعا ("he charged at me bravely"). However, when two parsings are equally possible in a word, one needing an implied element and the other not, then not implying is preferable.

safi-cedvel:153-153.t:
* I'rab:
(يسأل) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (أهل) fāʿil (agent), nominative; (الكتاب) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (تنزّل) an imperfect verb, subjunctive, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو" «[Translator's note: so in the source; since the verb addresses the Prophet ﷺ, the expected implied form is "anta".]»; (على) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تنزّل); (كتابا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (من السماء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تنزّل) «[Note: or to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (كتابا).]»; (الفاء) causal «[Note: it is permissible for it to be the connective of the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you consider what they asked enormous, then they asked Moses.."]»; (قد) a particle of realization; (سألوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma..
and the wāw is the fāʿil; (موسى) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (أكبر) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (من) a preposition; (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. And (اللام) for distance, and (الكاف) for address. [Translator's note: so in the source; ذلك here is governed by the preposition من.]
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تنزّل) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the verb يسألك.
(الفاء) conjunctive; (فقالوا) like سألوا; (أرنا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, and (نا) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنت"; (الله) the Name of Majesty, a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (جهرة) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative, standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), for it is a kind of seeing in general «[Note: it is permissible for it to be a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "they said that openly".]»; (الفاء) conjunctive, linking the effect to the cause; (أخذت) a past verb ... and (التاء) for the feminine, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الصاعقة) fāʿil, nominative; (بظلم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أخذتهم), and the bāʾ is causal, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (ثمّ) a conjunction; (اتّخذوا العجل) like سألوا موسى, and the second object is omitted, its implied form being "as a god"; (من بعد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (اتخذوا); (ما) a maṣdar-forming (maṣdarī) particle; (جاءتهم) like أخذتهم; (البيّنات) fāʿil, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما جاءتهم البيّنات) is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
(الفاء) conjunctive; (عفونا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, and (نا) a pronoun, fāʿil; (عن) a preposition; (ذلك) like the first, attached to (عفونا); (الواو) conjunctive; (آتينا) like عفونا; (موسى) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the alif; (سلطانا) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (مبينا) naʿt, accusative.
The clause «يسألك أهل ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تنزّل ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative.
The clause «سألوا ...» has no grammatical position, causal, for omitted speech, i.e. "do not mind their asking".
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause سألوا as an explicative conjunction.
The clause «أرنا ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «أخذتهم الصاعقة» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause قالوا.
The clause «اتّخذوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause أخذتهم الصاعقة.
The clause «جاءتهم البيّنات» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «عفونا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause اتّخذوا ...
The clause «آتينا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause عفونا.

safi-cedvel:154-154.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunctive; (رفعنا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn..
and (نا) a pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent); (فوق) an adverb of place, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (رفعنا), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الطور) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (بميثاق) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb (رفعنا), and the bāʾ is causal, i.e. "because of their breaking their covenant", and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunctive; (قلنا) like رفعنا; (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (قلنا); (ادخلوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الباب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (سجّدا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the fāʿil of ادخلوا; (الواو) conjunctive; (قلنا لهم) like the first; (لا) prohibitive, making the verb jussive; (تعدوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (في السبت) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تعدوا); (الواو) conjunctive; (أخذنا) like رفعنا; (منهم) like لهم, attached to (أخذنا); (ميثاقا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (غليظا) naʿt (adjective), accusative.
The clause «رفعنا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause آتينا «[Note: in the previous verse (153).]».
The clause «قلنا لهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause رفعنا.
The clause «ادخلوا ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The (second) clause «قلنا لهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the (first) clause قلنا.
The clause «لا تعدوا ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «أخذنا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause قلنا.

safi-cedvel:155-158.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (الباء) a preposition of causation; (ما) redundant (zāʾida); (نقض) genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being (لعناهم) «[Note: at the beginning of al-Māʾida the verb came stated explicitly; Allah the Exalted said: «فبما نقضهم ميثاقهم لعنّاهم ...» (verse 13).]», and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (ميثاق) the object of the maṣdar نقض, accusative (manṣūb), and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunctive; (كفرهم) like نقضهم and maʿṭūf (conjoined) on it; (بآيات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the maṣdar (كفر); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) conjunctive; (قتلهم الأنبياء) like نقضهم ميثاقهم; (بغير) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "wrongfully"; (حق) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) conjunctive; (قولهم) like نقضهم and conjoined on it; (قلوب) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (غلف) khabar (predicate), nominative; (بل) for transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī); (طبع) a past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative; (على) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (طبع); (بكفر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (طبع), and the bāʾ is causal, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) conjunctive, linking the effect to the cause; (لا) negating; (يؤمنون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (قليلا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), for it is its description «[Note: or a mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), because it stands in for the adverb, i.e. "a little time".. And it is not valid to make it an exception from the agent pronoun in يؤمنون, because these have had their hearts sealed; it may be valid to make it an exception from the pronoun in (عليها).]», accusative.
The implied clause «(لعنّاهم)» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «قلوبنا غلف» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «طبع الله عليها» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لا يؤمنون ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause طبع الله ...
(156) (الواو) conjunctive; (بكفرهم) like the first, attached to the implied verb لعنّاهم; (الواو) conjunctive; (قولهم) like كفرهم and conjoined on it; (على مريم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the maṣdar (قول), by its carrying the sense of their lying and their persisting, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, for it is a diptote; (بهتانا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative «[Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, for it is a kind of it, i.e. "their saying the saying of slander".]»; (عظيما) naʿt (adjective), accusative.
(157) (الواو) conjunctive; (قولهم) conjoined on the first قولهم, genitive like it; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (نا) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna; (قتلنا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.. and (نا) the fāʿil; (المسيح) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (عيسى) a badal (substitute) from المسيح, accusative like it, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (بن) a naʿt of عيسى, accusative like it, or a badal from it; (مريم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, for it is a diptote; (رسول) a naʿt of عيسى, accusative, or a badal from it, or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) «[Note: it is permissible for His saying (رسول الله) to be from the speech of Allah the Exalted and not from what they said, in praise of him; then the pause is on what precedes it, and رسول is accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "I praise".]»; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) resumptive; (ما) negating; (قتلوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) conjunctive; (ما صلبوه) like ما قتلوه; (الواو) conjunctive; (لكن) a particle of rectification (istidrāk); (شبّه) a past verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (شبّه); (الواو) conjunctive; (إنّ) like the first; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna; (اختلفوا) like قتلوا; (في) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (اختلفوا); (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), conveying emphasis; (في شك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of inna; (منه) like فيه, attached to a naʿt of شك; (ما) negating; (لهم) like the first, attached to a fronted khabar; (به) like فيه, attached to a ḥāl from علم; (من) a redundant preposition; (علم) genitive in form, nominative in position, as a delayed mubtadaʾ; (إلّا) a particle of exception; (اتّباع) the excepted, accusative in a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); (الظنّ) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) conjunctive; (ما قتلوه) like the first; (يقينا) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative, standing in for the maṣdar, for it is its description, i.e. "they did not kill him a certain killing" «[Note: it is permissible for it to be a ḥāl emphasizing the negation of the killing, i.e. "the killing is negated with emphatic certainty".]».
The clause «إنّا قتلنا ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl of the maṣdar قولهم.
The clause «قتلنا المسيح» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «ما قتلوه» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «ما صلبوه» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause ما قتلوه.
The clause «لكن شبّه لهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause ما قتلوه; and the clause «إنّ الذين اختلفوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause ما قتلوه.
The clause «اختلفوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «ما لهم به من علم» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) «[Note: or parenthetical, and the clause ما قتلوه يقينا is conjoined on the first clause ما قتلوه.]».
The clause «ما قتلوه ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined on the clause ما لهم به من علم.
(158) (بل) for invalidating digression (iḍrāb ibṭālī); (رفع) like طبع, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (إليه) like فيه, attached to (رفع); (الواو) conjunctive; (كان الله عزيزا حكيما) like كان الله سميعا عليما «[Note: in verse (148) of this sūra.]».
The clause «رفعه الله» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كان الله عزيزا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(نقض): an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb نقض ينقض, of the bāb نصر, its pattern فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(اتّباع): a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar of the five-letter verb اتّبع, its pattern افتعال, on the pattern of the past with kasra on the third letter and an alif added before the last.
(شكّ): an aural maṣdar of the verb شكّ يشكّ, of the bāb نصر, its pattern فعل with fatḥa then sukūn, and its ʿayn has been assimilated into its lām.
(يقينا): a resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from يقن ييقن, of the bāb فرح, its pattern فعيل.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ نِحْلَةً}: a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). It is the plural of «صَدُقة», with fatḥa on the ṣād and ḍamma on the dāl, on the pattern of «سَمُرة», and what is meant by it is the bridal gift (mahr). This is the well-known reading, and it is the dialect of the Ḥijāz. Qatāda read: «صُدْقاتهن», with ḍamma on the ṣād and sukūn on the dāl, plural of صُدْقة on the pattern of غُرْفة. Mujāhid and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it with ḍamma on both, and it is the plural of صُدُقة with ḍamma on the ṣād and the dāl, which is the "heavy" form of the one with a quiescent dāl, made for vowel harmony (itbāʿ). Ibn Waththāb and al-Nakhaʿī read: «صُدُقَتَهُنَّ», with ḍamma on both, in the singular. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the heavy form of «صُدْقة», like their saying «ظُلُمة» for «ظُلْمة»." We have already mentioned a disagreement: is it permissible to make "heavy" (vowel) a quiescent letter whose first radical has ḍamma? It was also read: «صَدْقاتِهن», with fatḥa on the ṣād and sukūn on the dāl, which is the lightened form of the well-known reading, like their saying عَضْد for عَضُد.

In the accusative of «نِحْلة» there are four views. First: it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), its governor being the verb before it, because «آتُوهُنَّ» has the meaning of «انحِلوهُنَّ» (give them freely); so it is a maṣdar not from the verb's own root (ʿalā ghayr al-ṣadr), as in «قَعَدْت جلوساً» (I sat down a sitting).

Second: it is a maṣdar standing in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial). As to the one whom the ḥāl describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl), there are three possibilities. First: it is the fāʿil (agent) in «فآتُوهُنَّ», i.e., "then give them, freely giving." Second: it is the first object, namely «النساء». Third: it is the second object, namely «صدقاتهن», i.e., "freely given."

The third view: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), if it is interpreted in the sense of «شِرْعة» (a prescribed law).

The fourth view: it is accusative by an implied verb with the meaning of "prescribed," i.e., "Allah has given this as a nihla," meaning He prescribed it as a law and a religion.

Al-niḥla: a gift given willingly; al-niḥla: a law (shirʿa) — and from this is «نِحْلة الإِسلام خير النِحَل» (the creed of Islam is the best of creeds), and "so-and-so yantaḥilu such-and-such," i.e., he professes it as a religion; and al-niḥla: an obligatory duty.

Al-Rāghib said: "Al-niḥla and al-naḥla: a gift given by way of voluntary generosity; it is more specific than a hiba (gift), since every niḥla is a hiba, but not the reverse. Its derivation, as I see it, is from al-naḥl (bees), with regard to their activity, as if «نَحَلْتُه» meant 'I gave him the gift of the bee.'" Then he said: "And it is possible that al-niḥla is the origin, and the bees were named that with regard to their activity." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "From 'he naḥala him such-and-such': he gave it to him and granted it to him willingly, niḥla and naḥl; and from this is the ḥadīth of Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him: 'I had given you (naḥaltuki) the harvest of twenty wasqs.'"

His words: «منه» are in the position of the genitive (majrūr), because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «شيء», so it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted word, i.e., "about something that is from it." As for «مِنْ» there, there are two views. First: it is partitive, and for that reason she may not give him the whole bridal gift; this was the view of al-Layth. Second: it is explicative (for clarifying the genus), and for that reason she may give him the whole bridal gift. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«مِنْ» here is for clarifying the genus, and for that reason she may give away the whole mahr; had it been partitive, that would not have been permissible." End of quote. It was mentioned above that al-Layth forbids that, so its being partitive presents no difficulty.

As for this pronoun, there are several views. First: it refers back to the bridal gift (al-ṣadāq) indicated by «صَدُقاتِهِنَّ». Second: it refers back to «الصَّدُقات» because the singular can fill its place: had it been said «صَداقَهُنَّ», the meaning would not have been disturbed. This resembles their saying: «هو أحسنُ الفتيان وأجملُه» (he is the finest of the young men and the handsomest of them [lit. "of it"]), because had it been said «هو أحسن فتىً» (he is the finest young man), the meaning would be correct. Similar to it is:

1539 - وطابَ ألبانُ اللِّقاح وبَرَدْ
(And the milk [pl.] of the milch-camels was good and became cool [sing.].)

In «برد» there is a pronoun referring back to «ألبان», because «لَبَن» (milk, sing.) can fill its place. Third: it also refers back to «الصَّدُقات», but by treating the pronoun the way a demonstrative is treated, for a demonstrative may, in the masculine singular, point to several things that preceded it, as in His words: {قُلْ أَؤُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِخَيْرٍ مِّن ذلكم} [Āl ʿImrān: 15], after He had mentioned several things before it. And you have already met, in al-Baqara, what is related about Ruʾba when he was asked about his words:

1540 - فيها خطوطٌ من سوادٍ وبَلَقْ ... كأنَّه في الجلدِ تَوْليعُ البَهَقْ
(In it are streaks of black and piebald white, as if it [masc. sing.] on the skin were the blotching of leucoderma.)

[He answered:] "I meant 'that'," so he treated the pronoun the way a demonstrative is treated. Fourth: it refers back to wealth (al-māl), even though it has not been mentioned, because the bridal gifts indicate it. Fifth: it refers back to the giving (al-ītāʾ) indicated by «آتُوا»; al-Rāghib and Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. Sixth: al-Zamakhsharī said: "The pronoun may be masculine so that it refers to the single bridal gift, and so it covers part of it; had it been feminine, its apparent sense would cover giving away the whole bridal gift, because 'part of the bridal gifts' is one of them or more." And the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "I say: what makes the masculine pronoun good is that the meaning of «فإنْ طِبْنَ» is 'if each one of them is pleased'; for that reason He said «منه», i.e., from her bridal gift. It is parallel to {وَأَعْتَدَتْ لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَئاً} [Yūsuf: 31], i.e., for each one of them, and for that reason He made «مُتَّكأً» singular."

His words: «نَفْساً» is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), and here it is transferred from the fāʿil, since the underlying form is "if their souls are pleased." Similar to it is: {واشتعل الرأس شَيْباً} [Maryam: 4]. This is accusative after the completion of the sentence. The tamyīz was brought here in the singular, even though a plural precedes it, because there is no ambiguity, since it is known that they do not all share in a single soul. Similar to it is: «قَرَّ الزيدون عيناً» (the Zayds were cool of eye), and «أنفساً» and «أعيناً» are also permissible. And we must touch on a rule of general benefit: when a tamyīz occurs after a plural, accusative after the completion of the sentence, then it is either in agreement in meaning with what precedes it or different from it. If it is the first, the tamyīz must agree with what precedes it, as in: «كَرُمَ الزيدون رجالاً» (the Zayds were noble as men), just as it agrees with it as a khabar (predicate), an adjective or a ḥāl.

If it is the second, then it either has a single referent or differing referents. If it has a single referent, the tamyīz must be singular, as you say of the sons of one man: «كَرُم بنو زيد أباً أو أصلاً» (the sons of Zayd were noble in father, or in origin), i.e., they all have one father who is characterised by nobility. Similar to it is: «كَرُم الأتقياءُ سَعْياً» (the pious were noble in endeavour), if you do not intend by the maṣdar a difference of kinds owing to the difference of those in whom it resides.

If it has differing referents, then either making the tamyīz singular would cause ambiguity or it would not. If it would cause ambiguity, agreement is required, as in: «كَرُم الزيدون آباء» (the Zayds were noble in fathers), i.e., each one has a father different from the other's father, characterised by nobility; had it been made singular here, it would be imagined that they are all the sons of one father, while the intent is the opposite. If it would not cause ambiguity, both are permissible, agreement and the singular, and the singular is preferable; for that reason the noble verse came in accordance with it. The ruling for the dual in this is like the plural.

What also made the singular good here is what was mentioned earlier as making the masculine and singular pronoun in «منه» good, namely that the meaning is: "if each one of them is pleased in soul." One of the Basrans said: "It was made singular only because what is meant by 'soul' here is desire (al-hawā), and desire is a maṣdar, and maṣdars are not made dual or plural." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«نفساً» is a tamyīz, and it is singular because the purpose is to state the genus, and the singular indicates it." Abū al-Baqāʾ took a similar line, and likened it to «درهماً» in your saying «عشرون درهماً» (twenty dirhams).

The grammarians disagreed about whether the tamyīz may be placed before its governor when the governor is a fully inflected (mutaṣarrif) verb. Sībawayh forbade it, while al-Mubarrad and a group allowed it, citing as evidence their saying:

1541 - أَتَهْجُرُ ليلى بالفراقِ حبيبها ... وما كان نفساً بالفراقِ تَطِيب
(Does Laylā forsake her beloved by parting, when she was never, in soul, content with parting?)

And his words:

1542 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . إذا عِطْفاه ماءً تَحَلَّبا
(... when his two flanks dripped with water [i.e., sweat].)

The underlying forms are «تطيبُ نفساً» and «تحلَّبا ماء». There is long discussion of the two verses which this is not the place for. Sībawayh's argument for forbidding it is that the tamyīz is in origin a fāʿil, and the fāʿil does not come first, and so likewise what is equivalent to it. This was objected to with «زيداً» in your saying «أخرجْتُ زيداً» (I brought Zayd out), for «زيداً» was in origin a fāʿil before the transfer, since the underlying form is «خرج زيد» (Zayd went out). But the difference is clear. The tamyīz has many types, mentioned in the books of the grammarians.

The two prepositional phrases in His words: «فإن طِبْنَ لكم عن شيءٍ» are attached to the verb before them, which is made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of turning away (from a claim); for that reason it is made transitive with «عَنْ», as if it were said: "if they turn away for you from something, willing in soul." The fāʾ in «فَكُلوه» is the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis) and it is obligatory, and the hāʾ in «فَكُلوه» refers back to «شيء».

His words: {هَنِيئاً مَّرِيئاً}: in the accusative of «هنيئاً» there are four views. First: it is accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, the implied form being "an eating that is wholesome." Second: it is accusative as a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «فكلوه», i.e., "made wholesome," that is, easy. Third: it is accusative as a ḥāl governed by a verb that may never be made overt at all, because this ḥāl is intended to substitute for its verb, as in «أقائماً وقد قعد الناس» (standing, when the people have sat down?), just as a maṣdar substitutes for its verb, as in «سُقْياً له ورَعْياً» (may he be watered and cared for). Fourth: they are two adjectives that have taken the place of a maṣdar intended for supplication which substitutes for its verb. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "One may pause at «فكلوه» and begin «هنيئاً مريئاً» as a supplication, on the view that they are two adjectives set in the place of two maṣdars, as if it were said: هَنْئاً مَرْءاً."

The Shaykh said: "This is a distortion of the grammarians' words, and his distortion is that he made them stand in the place of the maṣdar, so that their accusative is the accusative of the maṣdar; for that reason he said 'as if it were said: هَنْئاً مَرْءاً,' so that it became like your saying «سُقْياً لك» and «رَعْياً لك». What shows his distortion and the correctness of the grammarians' view is that maṣdars intended for supplication do not put an overt noun in the nominative: you do not say «سقياً الله لك» nor «رعياً الله لك», even though that is permissible with their verbs; whereas «هنيئاً مريئاً» do put an overt noun in the nominative, as evidenced by his words:

1543 - هنيئاً مريئاً غيرَ داءٍ مُخامِرٍ ... لعَزَّةَ مِنْ أَعْراضِنا ما استحَلَّتِ
(Wholesome and pleasant, no lingering malady, be to ʿAzza whatever of our honour she has deemed lawful.)

So «ما» is nominative through «هنيئاً» or through «مريئاً», by way of iʿmāl (two governors competing for one noun). That was permissible even though there is no link between the two governors by a conjunction or anything else, because «مريئاً» is only used as a follower of «هنيئاً», so the two are as one governor; had you said «قام قعد زيد», it would not be a case of iʿmāl except by intending a conjunction." End of quote.

However, there is in Sībawayh's wording what points to what al-Zamakhsharī said, for he said: "«هنيئاً مريئاً» are two adjectives whose accusative is the accusative of maṣdars used in supplication, by the verb whose overt use is not employed, elided because the speech indicates it, as if they said: 'that has become established, wholesome and pleasant'." So the beginning of the wording supports al-Zamakhsharī, while its end, namely his implied form "as if they said: 'that has become established, wholesome'," muddies it for him. So on the first two views «هنيئاً مريئاً» are connected to the sentence before them in wording and meaning, while on the last two they are cut off in wording, because their governor is implied from another sentence, as was established above.

The grammarians disagreed about your saying, to someone who said "So-and-so obtained good": «هنيئاً له ذلك» (wholesome to him be that): is «ذلك» nominative through the implied verb, the implied form being "that became established for him, wholesome," with «ثبت» elided and «هنيئاً», which is a ḥāl, taking its place; or is it nominative through «هنيئاً» itself, because when it took the place of the verb it put in the nominative what the verb would put in the nominative — just as in your saying «زيدٌ في الدار» (Zayd is in the house), «في الدار» [carries] a pronoun that was latent in "being settled" (al-istiqrār), and when "being settled" was elided and the prepositional phrase took its place, it put in the nominative the pronoun that had been in it? Al-Sīrāfī held the first view and placed in «هنيئاً» a pronoun referring back to «ذلك»; Abū ʿAlī held the second and made «هنيئاً» empty of a pronoun because it puts the overt noun in the nominative. If you say «هنيئاً» without saying «ذلك», then on al-Sīrāfī's view there is in «هنيئاً» a pronoun referring back to the one described by the ḥāl, which is the agent pronoun that was latent in the elided «ثَبَتَ»; and on al-Fārisī's view there is in «هنيئاً» a pronoun that is its fāʿil, which is the pronoun that was the fāʿil of «ثَبَتَ», and «هنيئاً» has taken the place of the elided verb, empty of a pronoun.

As for the accusative of «مريئاً», there are five views [Translator's note: only two are enumerated in the text as given]. First: it is an adjective of «هنيئاً»; al-Ḥūfī held this. Second: it is accusative in the same way as «هنيئاً», and the views about that have been mentioned above. Al-Fārisī rejected its being an adjective of «هنيئاً», saying: "Because «هنيئاً» has taken the place of the verb, and the verb is not qualified by an adjective, and likewise what takes its place." What supports al-Fārisī's statement is that the active participle, the passive participle, the intensive forms and maṣdars, when qualified by an adjective, do not govern as the verb does.

«مريئاً» was only used as a follower of «هنيئاً». Some reported that it may come not as a follower, but this is rejected, because the Arabs used it only as a follower. Are «هنيئاً مريئاً» in origin active participles on an intensive pattern, or are they two maṣdars that came on the pattern faʿīl, like al-ṣahīl (neighing) and al-hadīr (braying)? There is disagreement. The Shaykh transmitted the second view from Abū al-Baqāʾ, saying: "Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed them to be two maṣdars that came on the pattern faʿīl, like al-ṣahīl and al-hadīr, though they are not of the type in which faʿīl is regular for the maṣdar." End of quote. In Abū al-Baqāʾ's wording there is a difficulty, so we must touch on it so that what is in it may be known. He said: "«هنيئاً» came on the pattern faʿīl, and it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e., an eating that is wholesome. It was also said: it is a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl from the hāʾ, the implied form being 'made wholesome'; and «مريئاً» is like it. Al-marīʾ is faʿīl in the sense of mufʿil, because you say: 'the thing was pleasant to me (amraʾanī)'." The point of difficulty is: after ruling that they are maṣdars, how can he make them adjectives of an omitted maṣdar, and how can he explain «مريئاً», the maṣdar, in the sense of an active participle?

Al-Zamakhsharī held that they are adjectives; he said: "al-hanīʾ and al-marīʾ are two adjectives from 'the food was wholesome (hanuʾa)' and 'was pleasant (maruʾa)', when it goes down easily with nothing to spoil it." End of quote.

Hanā yahnā, without hamza, is also a second dialect form. One says: «هَنَأني الطعامُ ومَرَأني» (the food was wholesome and pleasant to me); if you use «مَرَأني» alone, it is only used as a four-letter verb, so you say «أَمْرأَني»; it is used as a three-letter verb only for symmetry with «هَنأَني». This is as they said: «أَخَذَه ما قَدُم وما حَدُث» (what was old and what was new seized him), with ḍamma on the dāl of «حدث» for symmetry with «قَدُم»; were it used alone, it would only be used with fatḥa on the dāl. It has other parallels. One says: «هَنَأْتُ الرجل أَهْنِئُه», with kasra on the middle radical in the imperfect, i.e., I gave him. The derivation of al-hanīʾ is from al-hināʾ, which is the tar with which a camel is smeared against mange. He said:

1544 - مُتَبَذِّلاً تَبْدُو محاسِنُه ... يَضَع الهِناءَ مواضِعَ النُّقْبِ
(Working in his everyday clothes, his fine qualities showing, he puts the tar on the spots of mange.)

Al-marīʾ: what goes down easily and smoothly in the throat; and from this the passage of food from the gullet to the mouth of the stomach was called al-marīʾ (the oesophagus).

semin-durr:5-5.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَلاَ تُؤْتُواْ السفهآء أَمْوَالَكُمُ}: the underlying form of «تُؤتوا» is «تُؤْتِيُوا», like «تُكْرِموا». The ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt to be heavy, so it was dropped; two quiescent letters then met, the yāʾ and the wāw of the pronoun, so the yāʾ was dropped so that two quiescent letters would not meet.

«السُّفهاء» is the plural of «سفيه» (foolish). It is reported from Mujāhid: "What is meant by 'the foolish' is women." Some considered this weak, on the grounds that faʿīla is only pluralised as faʿāʾil or faʿīlāt; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. But some have reported that «سفيهة» is pluralised as «سُفَهاء», like the masculine, and on this basis Mujāhid's view is not weak. The pluralisation of faʿīla as an adjective on fuʿalāʾ, though rare, has been reported for this word in particular. And Ibn ʿAṭiyya's restricting the plural of faʿīla to faʿāʾil or faʿīlāt is not evident, because «فِعال» is also regular in it, as in كَريمة / كِرام and ظَرِيفة / ظِراف. Likewise his stating faʿīla without qualification: he ought to have restricted it to where it is not in the sense of mafʿūla (passive meaning), to guard against «قتيلة» (one slain), for that is not pluralised as faʿāʾil.

The majority read {التي جَعَلَ الله لَكُمْ} in the singular form, as an adjective of «الأموال», even though it is a plural; because it has been mentioned more than once that for a plural of what is non-rational in the plural of multitude, or one that has only a single plural form, it is best to treat it as a feminine singular. «الأموال» is of this kind, because it is the plural of something non-rational and is only pluralised on afʿāl; though it has the form of a plural of paucity, what is meant by it is multitude.

Al-Ḥasan and al-Nakhaʿī read: «اللاتي», agreeing with the plural form. By analogy, only that whose singular is described by «التي» should be described by «اللاتي», and the singular of «الأموال», namely «مال», is not described by «التي». Al-Farrāʾ said: "The Arabs say «اللاتي» of women more than they say «التي», and of possessions they say «التي» more than they say «اللاتي». Both are permissible in both." It was also read «اللواتي», which is the plural of «اللاتي», and so a plural of a plural, or the plural of «التي» itself.

His words: «قياماً»: if we say that «جَعَلَ» means "made (into)" (ṣayyara), then «قياماً» is a second object and the first is omitted, namely the pronoun referring back to the relative noun, the implied form being "which He made it," i.e., made it for you a means of support (qiyām). If we say that it means "created," then «قِياماً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from that omitted referring pronoun, the implied form being "He made it," i.e., created it and brought it into being, in the state of being a support.

Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read: «قِيَماً», and the rest of the Seven: «قِياماً». Ibn ʿUmar read «قِواماً» with kasra on the qāf, and al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar «قَواماً» with fatḥa on it, and it is also transmitted from Abū ʿAmr. It was also read «قِوَماً», on the pattern of «عِنَب».

As for the reading of Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir, there are three views about it. First: «قِيَماً» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like «القيام» and not shortened from it; al-Kisāʾī, al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ said this. So it is a maṣdar in the sense of «القيام», by which firmness and permanence are meant.

This view was rejected on the grounds that the wāw ought to have remained sound, being protected by its medial position, just as the wāw of «عِوَض» and «حِوَل» remained sound. It was answered that it followed its verb in the weakening: just as its verb was weakened, so was it; and because it is in the sense of «القِيام», it was treated like it in the weakening. Al-Akhfash reported «قِيَماً» and «قِوَماً» and said: "Analogy requires the wāw to remain sound; it was weakened only irregularly, as in their saying «ثِيَرة» (bulls), and the Banū Ḍabba's saying «طِيال» as the plural of «طويل», and everyone's saying «جِياد» as the plural of «جَواد». And if they weakened «دِيَماً» because «دِيْمة» is weakened, then the weakening of a maṣdar because its verb is weakened is more fitting. Do you not see that the plural remains sound while its singular is weakened, in «معيشة» / «معايش» and «مقامة» / «مقاوِم», whereas they have not kept sound a maṣdar whose verb they weakened?"

Second: it is shortened from «قيام»; they dropped the alif for lightness, just as they said «خيَم» for «خِيام», and «مِخْيَط» and «مِقْول» for «مِخْياط» and «مِقْوال».
